title: RETRACTED: ch_spawn NO_COPY static lifetime conclusion
description: RETRACTED IN FULL - MY NINTH ERROR, AND A REPEAT OF A CLASS I NAMED IN THE SAME MESSAGE. I concluded from spawn.cc:275 (child_info_spawn NO_COPY ch_spawn) that "exec reuses a static whose constructor ran once", contrasted with forks stack-local frok grouped at fork.cc:626. THE STORAGE-CLASS FACT IS CORRECT; THE LIFETIME CONCLUSION IS FALSE. VERIFIED BY ME FROM PRIMARY SOURCE AFTER BEING CORRECTED, IN TWO LINES I ALREADY HAD IN FRONT OF ME: child_info.h:149 declares child_info_spawn () {} - AN EMPTY DEFAULT CONSTRUCTOR, so static-init mints nothing - and child_info.h:155 declares void set (child_info_types ci, bool b) { new (this) child_info_spawn (ci, b); } - PLACEMENT-NEW, so the REAL construction runs PER SPAWN into the statics storage. The base child_info.h:73 default ctor likewise only does parent (NULL). c63ab774 also measured it dynamically: CTOR type=1 parent=0x190 minted_in_pid=14816; CHILD got parent=0x190 usable=0 err=6 my_pid=24068 parent_winpid=14816 - minted per spawn, in the process that calls CreateProcessW, and the child receives EXACTLY the minted value. STORAGE CLASS IS STATIC; CONSTRUCTION IS PER-SPAWN. MY ERROR NAMED PRECISELY: I INFERRED CONSTRUCTION LIFETIME FROM STORAGE CLASS WITHOUT READING THE CONSTRUCTOR. I grepped the DECLARATION and never opened the class definition. AND IT IS THE SAME AXIS ERROR I HAD JUST NAMED ONE PARAGRAPH EARLIER - I wrote "configuration identity is not lifetime identity" and then immediately inferred lifetime from storage class. THE CORRECT GENERALISATION, SUPPLIED BY c63ab774: STORAGE CLASS IS NOT CONSTRUCTION LIFETIME EITHER. NO_COPY static storage with placement-new construction looks exactly like a long-lived object and is not one. Only instrumenting the mint settled it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD: the root cause is NARROWER and stranger than either of my candidates - a handle duplicated with bInheritHandle=TRUE, minted in the very process that calls CreateProcessW, passed bInheritHandles=TRUE, arriving in the child with the CORRECT NUMERIC VALUE, and still not present in the childs handle table.

description: VOID, reported as void. The committed Makefile.am note states "Windows on Arm MANDATES DYNAMIC_BASE" on the strength of my six-DLL result - but ALL SIX OF MINE WERE MICROSOFT SYSTEM DLLs (version, winmm, bcrypt, wintrust, cryptbase, profapi), so the generalisation to arbitrary images is broader than my evidence. I tried to close the gap using three non-system unsigned third-party ARM64 DLLs at the same DllCharacteristics 0x0160 (libwinpthread-1.dll, libintl-8.dll, libiconv-2.dll from gcc-native/driver-bin, all Machine=0xaa64, OptMagic=0x020b, Characteristics=0x2226, DLL bit set). Harness proven good by a same-code-path control: a copied stock system DLL LOADED while the third-party DLL FAILED err=193, so the fault is in the subjects not the instrument; those DLLs are unloadable for an unrelated and unexplained reason and I did NOT speculate about it. My measurement supports the mandate for Microsoft system DLLs; the only non-system corroboration is c63ab774 observation of msys-2.0-fixedbase.dll at 0x0100 failing err 193, which is theirs not mine. title: RETRACTED - my wild-value redirect was wrong
description: RETRACTED 2026-09-03. Raw bytes measured 00 A0 2C 00 80 00 00 00 = 0x80002CA000 = 512.0027 GiB AT FULL WIDTH. My one-hex-digit-wide hypothesis is FALSIFIED. THREE ERRORS, ALL MINE: (1) I claimed "nothing in Cygwin layout is at 512 GiB" - FALSE. MMAP_STORAGE spans 0x1000000000..0x700000000000 = 64 GiB..114,688 GiB and CONTAINS 512 GiB. I read the layout table as POINT VALUES when it is a table of RANGES, with the correct numbers in front of me. (2) The .003 was NEVER a fingerprint: 0x300000 = 0.00293 GiB and 0x2CA000 = 0.00272 GiB BOTH display as .003; it means only "~3 MB above a boundary". I built an identifier from a ROUNDED RENDERING instead of raw bytes - same class as reading one record of a multi-record file, a lossy representation treated as the thing itself. (3) My VirtualAlloc probe refuted nothing: it measured raw VirtualAlloc in a plain Win32 process while Cygwin mmap places allocations into MMAP_STORAGE by its own base selection - wrong mechanism, reported as though it bore on the question. CONSEQUENCE: the original ptmalloc/mmap-segment attribution IS consistent with the layout; my redirect was wrong and reached both the coordinator and 68c032ba; both corrected, artifact carries a retraction banner. THIS BREAKS THE PATTERN I ASSERTED ONE MESSAGE EARLIER: my four prior self-catches were INSTRUMENT bugs and I claimed my errors are always in the instrument not the reading. THIS WAS A REASONING ERROR and no harness precondition would have caught it; that claim was an over-generalisation from four points and is WITHDRAWN. SHAPE WORTH KEEPING: my redirect arrived INSIDE a correction of someone else work - exactly the "retraction is not self-limiting" position I had just warned 68c032ba about, occupied by me one hop later. A replacement explanation offered BY the corrector inherits MORE authority, not less. NEW RULES: never derive an identifier from a formatted/rounded value - fingerprints come from raw bytes; when a layout is expressed as RANGES, membership is a RANGE TEST. SCOPE OF RETRACTION: limited to the wild-value redirect. The malloc.cc:1670/1676 citation check, the verbatim layout constants, the x86_64 chain baseline, the 0x8000050B0 cross-check, the ASLR results and the installed-tree verification are unaffected.

title: BINDING — READ FIRST — classify a header set by whether a #define NORMALISES the struct tag, never by counting the identifier
description: BINDING RULE adopted 2026-09-03; the coordinator calls it the transferable output of the whole DISPATCHER_CONTEXT episode. CLASSIFY A HEADER SET BY WHETHER A #define NORMALISES THE STRUCT TAG — NEVER BY COUNTING OCCURRENCES OF THE IDENTIFIER. That single check FLIPPED TWO OF FIVE CLAIMED P25 SETS TO P19, INCLUDING MICROSOFT OWN SDK. VERIFIED FINAL CENSUS, each classification independently re-derived by me from the file rather than accepted: P25, meaning a genuine _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 tag with NO normalising define — (1) CLANGARM64 winnt.h, 405,341 bytes, sha256 51f9430b73aa131e9c966d5b701557adc090e6f51f93caf51bdc4a8f91f46f2c, struct at 2480, alias at 2496 under #if defined(_ARM64_); (2) mingw-w64 master, struct at 2465, ZERO normalising defines, verified by me. P19, meaning either no ARM64 identifier at all or a normalising define that rewrites the tag — (3) released w32api v12.0.0, no ARM64 identifier anywhere, three plain struct blocks; (4) Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 um\winnt.h, 876,232 bytes, normalising #define at 7101 bracketed by push_macro at 7099 and pop_macro at 7150; (5) widl winnt.h at C:\Users\crutkasLocal\.copilot\repos\mingw-w64\mingw-w64-tools\widl\include\winnt.h, 321,232 bytes, sha256 8841df7416bb11ec12e313489ea8c2124c66bc3aaa3d37328b4c2478a22bda19, normalising #define at 2030, declaration at 2072 whose tag that macro rewrites, undef at 2181 — the identical pattern to the SDK. SO THE FINAL COUNT IS TWO SETS TO P25 AND THREE SETS TO P19. THE OPERATIVE POINT SURVIVED EVERY REVERSAL, which is why the mechanism argument was the correct primary statement: TWO HEADER SETS IN ACTIVE USE GENUINELY PRODUCE P25 WITH NO NORMALISATION, therefore HARD-CODING EITHER VALUE IS UNSAFE, and the P19 token swap now sitting in the port tree STILL BREAKS against CLANGARM64 and mingw-w64 master. VERSION-ROBUSTNESS REMAINS MANDATORY. Record also that the earlier "five define it, two do not" was WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — it counted substrings AND misclassified two sets — which is a cleaner illustration of the failure mode than any of the three individual substring errors, because it shows the two errors compounding rather than cancelling.

title: BINDING HARD RULE — CORRECTED — x18 IS THE TEB ON WINDOWS ARM64; tpidr_el0 IS ZERO; NEVER WRITE x18
description: CORRECTED 2026-09-03 AFTER INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT. THE RULE AS PREVIOUSLY RECORDED WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE WRONG HALF WAS LOAD-BEARING — IT PROPAGATED INTO CODE AND CAUSED A REAL ACCESS VIOLATION. THE PREVIOUS WORDING SAID "read the TEB via tpidr_el0 (or read-only from x18); NEVER write x18". THE FIRST CLAUSE IS FALSE ON WINDOWS ARM64. CORRECT RULE, THREE PARTS: (1) x18 IS THE TEB POINTER ON WINDOWS ARM64 — READ THE TEB FROM x18. (2) tpidr_el0 IS ZERO ON WINDOWS ARM64 AND MUST NOT BE USED TO REACH THE TEB. (3) NEVER WRITE x18 — it remains the reserved platform register and a stray write is catastrophic; reading it is correct and required. MY OWN INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT, executed on this host inside my own process by assembling raw AArch64 instructions into allocated memory, flipping it to PAGE_EXECUTE_READ and calling it — no compiler involved: "mrs x0, tpidr_el0" returned 0x0000000000000000, ZERO; "mov x0, x18", encoded as orr x0, xzr, x18, returned 0x000000B179F55000; reading [x18 + 0x08] gave 0x000000D079B10000; and GetCurrentThreadStackLimits reported high = 0x000000D079B10000 — AN EXACT MATCH, which identifies x18 as pointing at a real TEB whose StackBase field is at offset 8. My absolute values differ from session c63ab774 measurements, as expected for a different process and thread, but THE RELATIONSHIP IS IDENTICAL AND REPRODUCES INDEPENDENTLY. THE CAUSAL CHAIN IS EXACT: the sequence "mrs xN, tpidr_el0" followed by "ldr xN, [xN, #8]" loads zero and then dereferences address 0x8, and the first captured fault from the execution attempt was an ACCESS VIOLATION READ with AV_TARGET_ADDRESS 0x0000000000000008 — a precise match between prediction and observed fault. WHERE THE BAD GUIDANCE LANDED: winsup/cygwin/include/cygwin/config.h __getreent(), and six trampoline emission sites in scripts/gendef, both of which followed the tpidr_el0 form. Session c63ab774 fixed both to read x18, and additionally REBUILT NEWLIB because the preserved libc.a and libm.a carried inlined __getreent copies compiled against the old header — an important second-order effect that a header-only fix would have missed. Reported result: tpidr_el0 occurrences in the linked DLL went 520 to 0, with 1,850 x18 sites. THE LESSON, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN THE EARLIER ONES: A RECORDED RULE CAN ITSELF BE WRONG, AND A WRONG RULE PROPAGATES FASTER AND FURTHER THAN AN UNRECORDED ASSUMPTION, BECAUSE IT CARRIES AUTHORITY. This one was written down, marked BINDING, honoured faithfully by two independent sessions, and produced faulting code in both. Rules that assert a machine-level fact must be measured before being recorded, not reasoned from architecture documentation — the generic AArch64 convention of tpidr_el0 as the thread pointer is simply not what Windows does.

title: BINDING — READ FIRST — pattern-matching failures need a MECHANICAL mitigation; recording a lesson does not prevent committing it
description:
BINDING RULE, and the durable finding of the session. RECORDING A LESSON DOES NOT PREVENT COMMITTING IT. I wrote the rule "read the script, do not grep it" ONE CYCLE BEFORE searching the pattern git\s+clone against a line that actually read git -c core.autocrlf=false clone — the words are non-adjacent, so my own freshly-recorded lesson did not stop me committing the exact error it described. FOUR DISTINCT PATTERN-MATCHING FAILURES THIS SESSION, all of the same family: (1) SHARED PREFIX — the substring git matching git-fsmonitor--daemon, and _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 matching _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64EC; (2) PREPROCESSOR REWRITING — counting textual occurrences of an identifier whose tag a #define rewrites, which inverted the answer rather than merely blurring it; (3) VARIABLE INDIRECTION — a value reached through a variable rather than appearing literally; (4) NON-ADJACENCY — intervening flags separating two words assumed to be adjacent. THE MITIGATION MUST BE MECHANICAL — A HABIT OR CHECKLIST STEP — NOT VIGILANCE. Concrete mechanical steps that would have caught these: use word-boundary or token-aware matching by default rather than substrings; when a symbol sits inside preprocessor conditionals, run the preprocessor instead of grepping; when checking whether a script does X, READ THE SCRIPT rather than pattern-matching it, because scripts are short and reading is cheap; and when a negative result would change a conclusion, state the exact pattern used so a reader can see what it would have missed. NOTED AS SHARED, NOT PERSONAL: the coordinator recorded making the same class of error four times today, including committing the substring error while cataloguing that exact class. Vigilance demonstrably fails against this family even for people actively thinking about it.

FIFTH INSTANCE, 2026-09-03T07:13Z, AND IT OCCURRED WITHIN MINUTES OF RECORDING THIS VERY RULE. I attempted a continuity edit anchored on the literal string "**output otherwise.** If the heartbeat suggests work..." and it FAILED TO MATCH. Cause: MARKDOWN LINE WRAP. The bold span actually opens on the PRECEDING line as "**Silence is the correct" and closes after "otherwise" on the next, so the real text is "...correct\noutput otherwise.**" and there is NO ** immediately before "output". I had assumed adjacency across a line break that does not exist. THIS IS THE SAME NON-ADJACENCY FAILURE AS THE git\s+clone CASE, committed AFTER writing the binding rule about it, which makes the point beyond argument: VIGILANCE DOES NOT WORK AGAINST THIS FAMILY, EVEN MINUTES AFTER DOCUMENTING IT. WHAT SAVED IT, AND THIS IS THE MECHANICAL MITIGATION WORKING AS DESIGNED: the script was written to ABORT AND WRITE NOTHING if the anchor did not match, so the failure was LOUD AND HARMLESS — a full replay immediately afterwards confirmed 60 PASS / 0 FAIL with no file modified. ADD TO THE MECHANICAL CHECKLIST: when anchoring a replacement in wrapped prose, ANCHOR ON A SHORT FRAGMENT THAT CANNOT SPAN A LINE BREAK, or read the target lines first and build the anchor from what is actually there rather than from what the rendered text appears to say. AND ALWAYS FAIL CLOSED: an anchored edit must abort and write nothing on mismatch, never fall through to a partial write.

title: BINDING — READ FIRST — for symbols inside preprocessor conditionals, measure what the COMPILER sees, never what grep finds
description: BINDING MEASUREMENT RULE adopted 2026-09-03, and it is the strongest vindication the mechanism-over-counting ruling will get. WHEN A SYMBOL APPEARS INSIDE PREPROCESSOR CONDITIONALS, THE ONLY VALID MEASUREMENT IS WHAT THE COMPILER SEES AFTER PREPROCESSING — NEVER WHAT GREP FINDS IN THE SOURCE TEXT. THE PROOF CASE: Microsoft Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 um\winnt.h contains SIX word-boundary occurrences of _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, which READS as strong support for the ARM64 tag being authoritative. IT IS THE REVERSE. Five of the six are plumbing — #pragma push_macro, #undef, #define _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, then #undef and #pragma pop_macro — and the sixth, the actual struct declaration at line 7130, HAS ITS TAG REWRITTEN BY THAT MACRO on any ARM64 target. NET EFFECT ON ARM64 IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE COUNT SUGGESTS: zero declarations survive as _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 and Microsoft mangles to P19. COUNTING DID NOT LOSE PRECISION HERE; IT PRODUCED THE OPPOSITE CONCLUSION. PRACTICAL METHOD: prefer running the preprocessor (cc -E, or compile a probe and read the symbol with nm) over grepping headers; where that is impossible, read every conditional guard enclosing each hit before drawing any conclusion. This subsumes and strengthens the earlier substring rule: word-boundary matching fixes only the ARM64-versus-ARM64EC class of error and would NOT have caught this one, because all six hits here are genuine token matches.

title: BINDING FOR EVERY SESSION — READ FIRST — always state the full absolute paths searched when reporting a negative
description: BINDING FOR EVERY SESSION IN THIS PROGRAMME, not just the coordinator or the continuity session, elevated 2026-09-03 at the coordinator request after it was observed that this single habit would have prevented BOTH failed searches for the CLANGARM64 header. title: URGENT CONTAMINATION MAP: 601 stale binaries, 3,829 tpidr_el0 encodings across /root/xc — inst is CLEAN, w-link is CLEAN
description: FULL ENCODING SCAN COMPLETED 2026-09-03. METHOD: scanned every .a .o .dll .exe .so .obj .lib file under /root/xc — 6,528 binaries — for the MRS Xt, TPIDR_EL0 instruction encoding 0xD53BD040 | Rt, matching the invariant little-endian byte sequence D0 3B D5 with the preceding byte constrained to 0x40-0x5F. This detects the defect IN COMPILED FORM, which reading corrected source cannot do. HEADLINE: 601 CONTAMINATED FILES CARRYING 3,829 STALE ENCODINGS. BY TREE: /root/xc/bld — 298 files, 1,676 encodings, AND THIS IS A SHARED TREE; /root/xc/w-autoload — 298 files, 1,676 encodings, an exact mirror since it configured from the same source; /root/xc/w-compose — 2 files, 236 encodings; /root/xc/w-orphans — 2 files, 236 encodings; /root/xc/w-gendef — 1 file, 5 encodings. CLEAN AND IMPORTANT: /root/xc/inst HAS ZERO CONTAMINATED FILES, so THE TOOLCHAIN SYSROOT ITSELF IS NOT AFFECTED — the compiler, binutils and target headers are fine and need no rebuild. /root/xc/w-link is likewise absent from the contaminated list, confirming it was genuinely rebuilt clean. /root/xc/w-implib and /root/xc/w-defects also show no contaminated binaries. WORST OFFENDERS: libg.a and libc.a at 406 encodings each in BOTH bld/newlib and w-autoload/bld/newlib; libdll.a at 231 in w-compose and 231 in w-orphans, and 226 in bld/winsup/cygwin and w-autoload/bld/winsup/cygwin; then individual objects strfuncs.o at 35, path.o at 22, kernel32.o at 18 and libc_a-getopt.o at 18. THREE FINDINGS THAT GO BEYOND WHAT WAS PREVIOUSLY KNOWN. FIRST, libg.a IS ALSO CONTAMINATED AT 406 and had not been identified — only libc.a and libm.a were previously named, so a rebuild targeting just those two would leave libg.a stale. SECOND, THE CONTAMINATION IS NOT CONFINED TO A FEW LIBRARIES: it spans 298 FILES PER TREE, overwhelmingly individual .o objects, so any partial or incremental rebuild risks leaving stale objects behind and only a full clean rebuild of newlib and winsup is safe. THIRD, AND MOST OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT, libdll.a IN BOTH w-compose AND w-orphans CARRIES 236 ENCODINGS EACH — these are the linkable runtime archives produced by those sessions, so ANY LINK PERFORMED FROM w-orphans OR w-compose WOULD SILENTLY REINTRODUCE THE TEB FAULT even with fixed sources and a fixed header. RESULTS, counts of MRS TPIDR_EL0 encodings present: /root/xc/bld/newlib/libc.a = 406 STALE; /root/xc/bld/newlib/libm.a = 3 STALE; /root/xc/w-autoload/bld/newlib/libc.a = 406 STALE; /root/xc/w-autoload/bld/newlib/libm.a = 3 STALE; /root/xc/w-link/bld/newlib/libc.a = 0 CLEAN; /root/xc/w-link/bld/newlib/libm.a = 0 CLEAN; /root/xc/w-link/bld/winsup/cygwin/new-msys-2.0.dll = 0 CLEAN; msys-2.0-teb.dll = 0 CLEAN; the earlier msys-2.0.dll = 520, which EXACTLY MATCHES the independently reported figure of 520 going to 0 and therefore corroborates that measurement precisely; and sigfe.s = 0. ANY SESSION THAT LINKS AGAINST /root/xc/bld/newlib/libc.a WILL SILENTLY REINTRODUCE THE TEB FAULT EVEN THOUGH THE SOURCE HEADER IS FIXED, because __getreent is inlined into every translation unit that used it and the object code is frozen in the archive. THIS IS THE STALE-BINARY TRAP IN ITS PUREST FORM: a source-level fix that is invisible in preserved object archives, where the defect survives in compiled form and no amount of reading the corrected header would reveal it. Session c63ab774 identified the mechanism and rebuilt newlib for its own tree; what this scan adds is that THE SHARED TREE WAS NOT REBUILT and remains contaminated. title: Owning the ASLR dynamicbase question programme-wide
description: ASSIGNED AND ACCEPTED. I am the single named owner of the ASLR/dynamicbase hypothesis; re-proposals route to me and may be refused flatly with the table rather than re-litigated. STANDING ANSWER, QUOTABLE: DllCharacteristics 0x0160 is correct and REQUIRED on Windows on ARM. Clearing DYNAMIC_BASE yields ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT (193) on 6 of 6 stock ARM64 system DLLs, with controls - pristine copy loads 6/6, byte-identical rewrite loads 6/6, checksum-zeroed still fails 6/6. HIGH_ENTROPY_VA is NOT mandated (clearing it alone still loads 5/6; the sixth is bcrypt failing signature validation for an unrelated reason). DLL ASLR is PER-IMAGE-PER-BOOT: an ASLR-enabled 0x4160 image loaded at one identical NON-PREFERRED base across 5 concurrent processes and 3 sequential loads, so relocation demonstrably occurred and parent and child share a base. CONTEXT: three independent derivations of --disable-dynamicbase so far. Coordinator identifies it as ONE INFERENCE FROM ONE ARTIFACT recurring at the rate people read the DLL header, not three minds agreeing, so correcting instances is unbounded work. THE RETRACTION IS NOT COMMITTED - it exists only in c63ab774 local uncommitted worktree, so a fresh clone never encounters it; coordinator escalating commit authority to the user. INTERIM MITIGATION I PROPOSED: the err 193 table should travel in any message touching DllCharacteristics so it propagates at roughly the rate the inference does. NORM EXTENSION I PROPOSED: "a session that refuses a directive with evidence is doing its job" needs its complement - WHOEVER ISSUES A DIRECTIVE OWES THE DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE ALREADY GATHERED AGAINST IT, since a session that never saw the table has nothing to refuse with and deference is then correct.

title: Using LF-safe git archive for identity work
description: STANDING RULE, CORRECTED AND SUPERSEDING the earlier over-generalised version. The autocrlf flag is operation-dependent: same flag, opposite correctness. (1) `git archive` -> ALWAYS use `-c core.autocrlf=false`; without it the export is silently CRLF-converted (the /usr/bin/perl + CR hazard). Verified: plain archive of winsup/autogen.sh gives 263 bytes / 13 CRLF / eaf4e90f..., versus 250 bytes / 0 CRLF / 4b21ed0f... with the flag. (2) `git diff` -> ALWAYS use the REPOSITORY DEFAULT; never force autocrlf=false. System core.autocrlf=true means the INDEX is LF and the WORKTREE is CRLF, and git diff applies that normalisation so the two are comparable; forcing the flag removes it and yields a degenerate WHOLE-FILE patch. Coordinator reproduced both forms independently on the live ABI worktree: default diff = 29 files, 785 insertions, 51 deletions; forced autocrlf=false = 29 files, 13,736 insertions, 13,002 deletions. Rule of thumb: use the flag when EXPORTING bytes, never when COMPARING against the index. (3) An unvalidated patch artifact is NOT evidence. A first backup was silently corrupted when PowerShell Set-Content -NoNewline collapsed it to a single line (727 KB, 1 diff header, ZERO changed lines) and was caught only by git apply --check --reverse. Always use `git diff --output=<file>`; never pipe patch text through the PowerShell pipeline. Preferred validation is a round-trip: extract a pristine base, apply, and compare every file. For identity work still prefer binding blob OID plus sha256 of blob bytes, which is export-independent; corrections must record both old and new values.

title: Verifying the cygheap corruption reframe
description: ASSIGNED, NOT STARTED. Claim to verify: fork is not a fork bug - every ARM64 MSYS2 process runs with a corrupt cygheap allocation chain and nothing notices because fork is the only code that walks it. Rests on: sizeof(init_cygheap)=0x48A0, offsetof(chain)=8, first entry at cygheap+0x68F0 past the header; and a deliberately-never-forking program reproducing the identical signature (unterminated chain, out-of-heap prev at the same entry). LIVE LEAD WITH DISCONFIRMING EVIDENCE ATTACHED: cygheap initially points at an 8-byte cygheap_dummy typed as init_cygheap whose chain is at offset 8, so any early touch lands one word past it - BUT that code is IDENTICAL ON x86_64 WHERE FORK WORKS, so the dummy alone cannot be the explanation. Decisive test: does anything reach _cmalloc EARLIER on ARM64? Static constructors are the prime suspect because THE CTOR LIST WAS BROKEN UNTIL TODAY, so constructors now run that previously could not. NOTE the ordering trap: geometry constants must be verified against the SAME BUILD that produced the corruption signature, given artefacts are being rebuilt every few minutes.

title: Applying texinfo workflow dependency fix
description: CANONICAL ACCOUNT, corrected 2026-09-03 after synthesis of two independent analyses. THE FAILURE IS NOT "makeinfo is missing". IT IS "THE EXISTING makeinfo STUB IS INEFFECTIVE AND NEVER REACHES THE BUILD ENVIRONMENT." The old wording is actively harmful: it would send an investigator to add a stub that is ALREADY THERE AND ALREADY DEAD. COORDINATOR-VERIFIED FACT: .github/scripts/enable-ccache.sh already contains, on BOTH origin/main AND PR #10 HEAD, at line 37 pushd /usr/lib/ccache/bin, line 39 export MSYS=winsymlinks, line 43 if [[ "$FLAVOR" = "CROSS" ]]; then, line 44 ln -sf /usr/bin/true makeinfo. The CI log proves this executed at 01:37:13 and yet configure still reported "checking for makeinfo... no" at 01:40:32, so the stub never reaches the build environment; its visibility depends on makepkg ccache BUILDENV PATH injection. SYNTHESIS: main has NEITHER a working stub NOR texinfo, so it fails. The PR #1 branch carried texinfo and therefore passed REGARDLESS of the broken stub. The stub finding explains WHY the stub route cannot be trusted; the A/B finding proves WHICH route is empirically green. Neither alone is sufficient: the stub finding alone could have led to repairing a stub that fakes documentation with /usr/bin/true, and the A/B alone would have left dead misleading code in place. CONVERGENCE IS THE STRONGEST SIGNAL AVAILABLE: adding real texinfo is simultaneously the most principled fix (the current approach fakes docs with /usr/bin/true) and the only empirically proven-green fix. Two independent paths, same answer. SECONDARY ACTION, to be part of the same eventual change: enable-ccache.sh:44 should be REMOVED OR REPAIRED rather than left as misleading dead code. FLAGGED NOT ASSERTED, do not investigate now: export MSYS=winsymlinks at line 39 omits a mode suffix, whereas MSYS2 expects :lnk, :native, :nativestrict or :sysfile, so it may be a silent no-op; this is a hypothesis, not a finding. STILL PENDING AUTHORITY: neither the texinfo addition nor the stub cleanup is to be applied; both need commit authority the owner has not granted.

title: DEFECT in the sealed port: hard-coded ARM64 SEH handler name is wrong for pinned w32api v12.0.0
description:
SEALED-PORT DEFECT, found by session c63ab774 and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE COORDINATOR, 2026-09-03. winsup/cygwin/local_includes/exception.h and local_includes/cygtls.h HARD-CODE the mangled SEH handler name ...P25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 on the assumption that ARM64 winnt.h names the struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64. THAT ASSUMPTION IS FALSE FOR THE PINNED w32api v12.0.0. COORDINATOR VERIFICATION: v12.0.0 winnt.h is 10390 lines and contains THREE plain "struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT" definitions at 2074-2078, 2310-2314 and 2974-2978, one per architecture block, with the identifier _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 ABSENT FROM THE ENTIRE FILE. By contrast mingw-w64 MASTER does define _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 at line 2465 and aliases DISPATCHER_CONTEXT to it at 2481, so the name genuinely differs BY HEADER VERSION. CONSEQUENCE UNDER v12.0.0: exceptions.o demonstrably defines ...P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, so the .seh_handler directive names a symbol THAT NEVER EXISTS. The failure is SILENT and LINK-TIME-ONLY, which is exactly the kind that survives review. FIX SHAPE — EXPLICITLY *NOT* A ONE-TOKEN FIX, AND MUST NOT BE RECORDED AS ONE. The link session first described it as a single token in each of two files and the coordinator has since corrected that. Swapping P25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 for P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT would fix released w32api v12.0.0 AND THEN BREAK under any header set that DOES define _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 — INCLUDING THE CLANGARM64 TOOLCHAIN THIS PROGRAMME ALSO USES, whose winnt.h carries 2 occurrences of it. A token swap therefore REINTRODUCES THE IDENTICAL BUG IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION. THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THAT THE PORT HARD-CODES A MANGLED NAME AT ALL, which makes .seh_handler silently header-version-dependent with the failure deferred to link time. THE FIX MUST BE VERSION-ROBUST: derive the name, or condition on whether the struct exists. Record it this way so nobody applies a token swap. NOT AUTHORIZED TO FIX — recorded as located, not scheduled. This is the highest-value finding of the link attempt.

SCOPE EXPANDED 2026-09-03, CONFIRMED BY THE COORDINATOR: THE VERSION-ROBUST FIX MUST ALSO DELETE TWO FALSE COMMENTS, because the drift is a bigger problem than the token. exception.h:16-18 now ASSERTS "plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT on every architecture — there is no _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64", which is FALSE AS A UNIVERSAL and is stated with the confidence of settled design; the CLANGARM64 header defines exactly that struct and aliases it under #if defined(_ARM64_). And cygtls.h:365 STILL CLAIMS THE OPPOSITE while the code three lines later emits P19 — comment and code contradicting each other inside the same file. Both comments must go as part of the fix. STILL OWNER-AUTHORISED AND NOT TO BE STARTED.

title: GAP: gendef gates all trampoline emission on x86_64 so sigfe.s is 0 bytes on aarch64

THE FILE CONTAINS ZERO OCCURRENCES OF aarch64. Consequence: on aarch64 every gated block is skipped and SIGFE.S IS GENERATED AT 0 BYTES — no signal-frame trampolines at all. This corroborates the sealed ABI session finding that after its work exactly ONE "#error unimplemented for this target" site remained, and that it was the gendef-generated sigfe.s. REMAINING GAP LIST BESIDES THIS: autoload.cc carries x86-only thunk assembly; the 10 missing aarch64/*.S routines; thread.cc:1977 fails with unknown mnemonic pause; and 5 math long-double sites. NEWLY IDENTIFIED AND NOT IN THE SEALED PORT: newlib/libc/include/sys/config.h:7 defines MALLOC_ALIGNMENT 16 for ALL __aarch64__ targets, colliding with Cygwin own ((size_t)16U) definition — an aarch64-only -Werror collision that ALONE blocked 7 objects including dcrt0, fork, pinfo and mm/malloc*. title: PRESERVATION GAP: sigfe.o is listed in the handoff manifest but is NOT present
description: MEASURED DISCREPANCY 2026-09-03, found by checking the handoff manifest against the filesystem rather than by validating any technical claim. THE REPORT STATES "All files in session-state/7be14c31.../files/: gendef, sigfe.s, sigfe.o, tlsoffsets, RESULT.md". THE DIRECTORY ACTUALLY CONTAINS gendef 23,256 bytes, RESULT.md 9,125 bytes, sigfe.s 294,545 bytes, sigfe.s.sha256 148 bytes and tlsoffsets 1,822 bytes. sigfe.o IS ABSENT. The report elsewhere describes sigfe.o as pe-aarch64-little at 151,917 bytes with 990 global symbols, so the object was produced but was NOT PRESERVED. ASSESSMENT: THIS IS LOW SEVERITY AND NOT A DATA LOSS, because sigfe.o is DERIVABLE by assembling the preserved sigfe.s, and sigfe.s.sha256 is present to bind that source. It matters as a MANIFEST ACCURACY problem: a successor reading the manifest would expect an object that is not there, and would not immediately know whether it was lost or never preserved. THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE EARLIER "LISTING IS NOT PRESERVING" FINDING, in a milder form — there the README listed a toolchain prefix it did not contain; here a manifest lists an object it does not contain. RECOMMENDED, NOT DONE AND NOT AUTHORISED: either preserve sigfe.o alongside sigfe.s, or amend the manifest to state that the object is derivable from the preserved assembly and is deliberately not kept. I did not modify that session artifacts, since the directory belongs to it and I am stood down.

title: CANDIDATE IOU (INVESTIGATION-ONLY, NOT AUTHORISED): propose mingw-w64 headers adopt the normalisation the SDK and its own widl already perform
description: RECORDED 2026-09-03 AS A HYPOTHESIS WITH GOOD SUPPORTING EVIDENCE, EXPLICITLY *NOT* AS AN ESTABLISHED DEFECT, AND NOT AUTHORISED TO BE RAISED WITH ANYONE. THE REFRAMING THAT PRODUCED IT: Microsoft is DELIBERATELY MAKING THE MANGLED NAME ARCHITECTURE-INDEPENDENT. The push_macro/pop_macro bracketing scopes the rewrite to exactly the struct definition, so the TYPEDEF name stays DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 at SDK line 7143 while the underlying TAG becomes _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. That is engineering effort spent for a specific outcome, not an accident. The census therefore stops being "2 versus 3" and becomes A CONFORMANCE QUESTION, with P25 as THE DEVIATION rather than a co-equal spelling — the first principled reason to prefer one value over the other, and it required running the mechanism check to completion to reach. THE SHARPENING, PROVEN BY ME FROM A SINGLE CHECKOUT AT A SINGLE COMMIT: WIDL IS PART OF MINGW-W64, so MINGW-W64 IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT. In C:\Users\crutkasLocal\.copilot\repos\mingw-w64 at commit b0c3cce6a14965dbac1713e619c811a149044dcd (2026-08-27), mingw-w64-headers/include/winnt.h is 415,567 bytes with ZERO normalising defines and a genuine declaration at 2465, giving P25; while mingw-w64-tools/widl/include/winnt.h is 321,232 bytes with a normalising define at 2030 and its declaration at 2072 rewritten by it, giving P19. SAME PROJECT, SAME COMMIT, TWO COPIES OF winnt.h, TWO DIFFERENT TREATMENTS OF THE SAME IDENTIFIER. An external divergence from Microsoft could plausibly be deliberate; AN INTERNAL DISAGREEMENT INSIDE ONE PROJECT IS MUCH HARDER TO EXPLAIN AS A CHOICE, which is the strongest single argument that the headers omission is an oversight. THIS ALSO RESOLVES A DISCREPANCY I HAD FLAGGED: the coordinator 415,567-byte figure is the LOCAL CHECKOUT, whereas my earlier 404,786 was the GitHub raw master — different commits of the same file, not conflicting measurements. MANDATORY CAUTION: mingw-w64 may have a reason not yet found. ARM64EC interactions, or a deliberate choice to keep the ARM64 struct distinct for cross-architecture tooling, are both plausible. BEFORE ANYTHING IS CLAIMED UPSTREAM SOMEONE MUST CHECK MINGW-W64 HISTORY AND ANY DISCUSSION AROUND IT. INVESTIGATION FIRST; NO CONTRIBUTOR CONTACT; NOT AUTHORISED.

title: OPEN, NOT DIAGNOSED: second fault after the TEB fix is a branch to 0xFFFFFFFF00000000
description: RECORDED 2026-09-03 as an open item, reported as-is by session c63ab774 and NOT diagnosed by me. After the TEB fix the child still dies with 0xC0000005 but THE FAILURE MOVED, which is itself evidence the first fix was real. New fault: ACCESS_VIOLATION EXEC with target 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 at PC 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 — THE PROGRAM COUNTER ITSELF IS THE BAD VALUE, so this is a branch to a corrupt code pointer rather than a null dereference. Two subsequent faults in the same capture are ACCESS_VIOLATION READ of the same target 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 at PC 0x00007FFDB4733FC4, module base 0x00007FFDAD3D0000, RVA 0x7363FC4. OBSERVATION OFFERED AS HYPOTHESIS ONLY, NOT ASSERTED: the value 0xFFFFFFFF00000000 has ALL HIGH 32 BITS SET AND ALL LOW 32 BITS CLEAR, which is the shape produced when a 64-bit pointer is assembled from a 32-bit all-ones value shifted left by 32, or when only the upper half of a pointer is written and the lower half left zero, or when a relocation or pointer patch writes the high half and never completes the low half. That is consistent with the session own suggestion that the autoload thunk mechanism, which rewrites function pointers at first call and is the next thing dll_entry exercises, is implicated — but it is equally consistent with several other mechanisms and I have NOT tested it. NEXT DIAGNOSTIC I WOULD RUN, not yet performed: identify what sits at RVA 0x7363FC4 in the DLL to name the faulting function, and inspect the autoload thunk patch sequence for a movz/movk chain that writes the high half before the low. NOT A REGRESSION: the runtime still maps and binds, and the fault has simply advanced further into initialisation.

title: CLOSING FINDING: a credit ledger that forces exclusivity destroys the value of redundant verification
description: JOINTLY ARRIVED AT AND RECORDED WITH JOINT ATTRIBUTION, which is itself the demonstration. MY HALF: authorship and primacy are different claims and the ledger had one slot for both, so apparent conflicts between threads were often INDEPENDENT CO-DISCOVERY rather than contradiction - and a later reader would have read "their claims conflicted" as "someone was wrong", an unfair inference caused by the record rather than by anything either thread did. THE COORDINATOR HALF, WHICH IS THE SHARPER STATEMENT: PARALLEL VERIFICATION THREADS ARE SUPPOSED TO PRODUCE THE SAME FINDING TWICE FROM SEPARATE MEASUREMENTS. That redundancy is precisely why the exec root cause survived contact with reality, and the instruction decode, the masking result and the hookapi cause were each independently arrived at more than once. SO A CREDIT LEDGER THAT FORCES EXCLUSIVITY TURNS THE PROGRAMME SINGLE MOST VALUABLE PROPERTY INTO AN APPARENT INCONSISTENCY. That is a much sharper criticism of the instrument than "the coordinator kept getting it backwards", and it means the decision to stop per-item attribution stands ON THE CORRECT GROUND - the shared-identity defect alone - and NOT on the parties disagreeing, because they largely did not disagree; the instrument could not represent what both were saying. MY OWN AUDIT OF THE TWO CONTESTED ITEMS IS THE WORKED EXAMPLE: pure-Win32 replication KEPT as authorship because I executed it with visible output in my own record; (status>>8)&0xff primacy CONCEDED because I cannot establish I was first. title: Programme doctrine: verify exec by exit status, never by captured output
description: MEASURED ON execfix.dll 8ffe979b, AND IT WOULD PRODUCE A FALSE NEGATIVE ON A WORKING FIX. THE EXECD SUCCESSOR STDOUT DOES NOT REACH A REDIRECTED STDOUT, WHILE ITS EXIT STATUS PROPAGATES CORRECTLY. Reproduced under TWO INDEPENDENT REDIRECTION ROUTES - Start-Process inherited handles and cmd.exe > redirection - byte-identical result. TIMING HYPOTHESIS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, not accepted: settle delays of 0, 1500 and 3000 ms produced byte-identical output, so it is NOT a race with the successor process; I proposed that mechanism and killed it myself. CLEAN DIFFERENTIAL THAT LOCALISES IT: a FORKED child output DOES survive the same redirection - the [child] forked child alive line appears - so the loss is specific to the exec path. CONSEQUENCE: A TEST THAT VERIFIES EXEC BY LOOKING FOR THE EXECD IMAGE PRINTED BANNER WOULD CONCLUDE THE CHILD NEVER RAN, ON A BUILD WHERE EXEC DEMONSTRABLY WORKS. Same family as the (status>>8)&0xff trap and the fail-open guards: VERIFY EXEC BY EXIT STATUS, NOT BY CAPTURED OUTPUT, and design fixtures so the exit code carries the whole result (mine encodes 42 intact / 43 missing / 44 corrupted). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this is pre-existing Cygwin behaviour, specific to this build, or specific to non-console stdout. Bounded observation only.

title: Programme doctrine: the shifted wait-status form hides signal deaths
description: ADOPTED AS PROGRAMME DOCTRINE 2026-09-03, measured by me and pushed to c63ab774 to audit its own fixtures. ANY TEST THAT COMPUTES (status >> 8) & 0xff ALONE SILENTLY REPORTS A SIGNAL DEATH AS EXIT CODE 0. Measured instance: on DLL 90bfb483 a fork+exec child was killed by SIGNAL 11, raw wait status 0x0b; p4exec duly printed "child exit code = 0 (expected 42)". The child never reached its _exit(99) at all. THIS SINGLE INSTRUMENT DEFECT EXPLAINS THE ENTIRE DISAGREEMENT THAT CONSUMED THREE PARTIES TONIGHT - it is how "the fixture reports exit 99" and "execl returns" entered the briefing I was given, both of which I refuted by measurement. CORRECT FORM: test the low 7 bits for a signal (status & 0x7f) and only interpret (status >> 8) & 0xff as an exit code when those bits are clear; print the RAW status either way. My own fixture printed the raw status, which is the only reason I caught it. GENERAL SHAPE, same family as the fail-open guards: a decoder that maps two distinct outcomes onto one value cannot distinguish them, and will report the benign one.

title: Governance rule: boundary not slope for scope of authorised work
description: RAISED BY ME AND ADOPTED BY THE COORDINATOR 2026-09-03, replacing its own framing. The coordinator authorised committing a fork fix PLUS the ~16-line #elif defined(__aarch64__) arm it lives in, on the reasoning that this was "the minimum enclosing scope of an already-authorised fix". MY OBJECTION, ACCEPTED: MINIMAL IS NOT THE RIGHT TEST, BECAUSE IT LICENSES EXPANSION INDEFINITELY - it is a SLOPE. THE RIGHT TEST IS A BOUNDARY: WOULD THE USER RECOGNISE THIS AS THE THING THEY AUTHORISED? On substance an #elif defined(__aarch64__) arm IS NEW ARCHITECTURE SUPPORT, not merely the enclosing scope of a bug fix, and the user had declined port work. The coordinator conceded it framed it the easy-to-authorise way, which is the reasoning it should distrust in itself. DECISION STILL STANDS on the mitigations - user unavailable, branch only, no PR, trivially revertable - but MY REMEDY WAS ADOPTED: the REASONING and not merely the SCOPE must live next to the commit, because a conversation-resident justification does not reach whoever reads the diff cold. THAT IS THE SAME LESSON AS THE --disable-dynamicbase RETRACTION, which is now the third independent time it has been learned, and it applies to governance decisions exactly as it does to technical claims.

title: Rule: a hash from a live path is not a valid label for a measurement
description: ADOPTED AFTER IT FIRED ON ME. I hashed the live path (9fcc134e), then copied, and THE COPY HASHED 227598ad - the path had been rewritten between the two operations, seconds apart. I did NOT report corruption; I separated the hypotheses first. MEASURED RESOLUTION: the copy differs from the source in EXACTLY 3 BYTES at contiguous offsets 3595818-3595820, a timestamp field; and a repeat-copy control was 3/3 MATCH, proving the WSL/drvfs copy path is clean. So I had transiently captured a genuine SECOND BUILD, not a corrupt file. THE RULE: COPY FIRST, HASH THE COPY, TEST THE COPY, RE-HASH THE COPY. A hash read from a path that another session is actively rewriting is not a valid label for anything, because the thing you hashed and the thing you tested are different objects. HAD I NOT COPIED-THEN-HASHED I WOULD HAVE PUBLISHED EXEC RESULTS LABELLED 9fcc134e THAT WERE ACTUALLY MEASURED ON 227598ad. INCIDENTAL AND USEFUL TO OTHERS: this accidentally and independently reproduces the reported "two relinks of the identical command differ in three bytes" finding, from a third party and by accident, which is stronger corroboration than a deliberate re-run. Functionally the two builds are the same program.

title: Adopting explicit supersession marking on cross-session corrections

This time the stale item was my own "x86_64 b=0 is unreconciled and should not be relied on until explained" - which I had ALREADY explained (buckets[23]=0x8000068f0, block is freed, union holds ptr=NULL, true size 98,304 = bucket_val[23] by span test). Three crossings in one thread is enough to stop treating it as bad luck. RELATED EARLIER LESSON: a conditional is only safe if its resolution travels as fast as the condition did; this is the same channel failure in a third form. CORRECTED TEXT GIVEN THEM: the ARM64 b=6 vs x86_64 0 comparison is NOT index-vs-index and may reflect allocated-vs-freed state at sample time; the span test settles it on ARM64 without touching the union. UNCHANGED THROUGHOUT: 0x8000068F8 should hold 0x8000068C0, since prev lives at +8 and survives free.

title: Auditing the tlsoffsets and sigfe generator guards
description: PRIMARY-SOURCE READ of the PRISTINE SEALED tree only; the live /root/xc/w-link tree is NOT reachable from here and nothing here is a claim about it. (1) CONFIRMED the heartbeat mechanism and locations exactly: scripts/gentls_offsets (3251 B, 40 identical copies) matches /\s*\.long\s+/ at LINES 65 AND 88, with a separate /\s*\.space\s*4/ branch at line 81. (2) MEASURED - THE SCRIPT ONLY GUARD FAILS OPEN. Lines 103-109 compute MOD from _cygtls.context_p; if the .long branch never fires that symbol is absent, MOD is EMPTY, and [ -ne 0 ] is a unary-operator error returning 2, so the if is FALSE. Executed under bash 5: MOD=[], BRANCH_NOT_TAKEN, stderr "[: -ne: unary operator expected", FINAL EXIT CODE 0. The file is NOT deleted and the script reports SUCCESS. Consequence: c63ab774 external before/after sha check was not belt-and-braces, it was THE ONLY THING on that path capable of catching the corruption. (3) FLAGGED CONTRADICTION, NOT ESTABLISHED THAT THE HAZARD MATERIALISED: gentls_offsets emits const uint32_t at lines 22 and 44, i.e. FOUR-BYTE objects, so a probe measuring a 64-bit long (.xword) measured the WRONG WIDTH and a fix keyed on .xword would silently still fail; moreover a tlsoffsets reported as 1822 B intact and good is POSITIVE EVIDENCE THAT .long WAS MATCHED, since a file whose .long branch never fired would be degenerate (only .space 4 members, all zero). Cheap resolution: compile extern "C" const uint32_t x = 42; with the aarch64 cross-compiler and read the directive. (4) NEW, NINTH x86-ONLY CONSTRUCT: scripts/gendef (11360 B, 485 lines) gates on my $is_x86_64 = $cpu eq x86_64 at line 24 with branches at 92, 97, 113, 350. In fefunc lines 88-111 $res is assigned ONLY inside if ($is_x86_64), so on any other cpu it stays UNDEF for every symbol with NO die, NO #error, NO warning. Critically .include "tlsoffsets" is ITSELF inside the x86_64 guard at line 115, so in the pristine generator an aarch64 build NEVER CONSUMES tlsoffsets at all and emits a degenerate sigfe.s with exit 0. Body is pure x86_64: leaq, movq, %r10-%r15, xchgl, xaddq, cpuid, fxsave64. .\x86_64 is the ONLY arch directory; there is NO aarch64 directory. Corroborates the standing finding that the sealed port was never link-capable for aarch64 and implies the live tree carries an UNARCHIVED gendef modification. STANDING OBSERVATION: BOTH generators on the tlsoffsets/sigfe path FAIL OPEN WITH EXIT 0; neither can detect its own failure.

title: Auditing the two items the ledger recorded as contested between me and 290c9aaf
description: AUDITED AGAINST MY OWN RECORD, AND THE RESULT SPLITS. The coordinator named two items where I claim authorship and 290c9aaf assigns them elsewhere citing contemporaneous entries. (1) THE PURE-WIN32 REPLICATION OF sigproc.cc:938 - I CAN EVIDENCE THIS DIRECTLY AND I MAINTAIN IT. I built the probe, ran it in this session, and the execution output is in my own record: exec set perms=0x101018 and fork set perms=0x101058, both returning GetHandleInformation flags=0x1 HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT SET, child valid at the same value with flags=0x1, ReadProcessMemory OK 64 bytes pattern A0-A7 intact. That is not a ledger claim, it is a thing I executed with visible output. (2) THE (status>>8)&0xff SIGNAL-DEATH FINDING - I CONCEDE PRIMACY AND KEEP ONLY INDEPENDENT DERIVATION. I measured raw status 0xb myself and reported the decode consequence from my own run; but 290c9aaf 23:12 entry attributes the FINDING to the main session with the REPAIR as its own, and its entry predates any ledger. I CANNOT ESTABLISH THAT I FOUND IT FIRST AND I AM NOT GOING TO ASSERT IT. THE REFINEMENT THIS PRODUCES, AND IT IS THE USEFUL PART: THE LEDGER CONFLATED AUTHORSHIP WITH PRIMACY. Those are different claims. Two parties can independently produce the same finding from separate measurements - which is exactly what a programme running parallel verification threads should EXPECT and even want - and a per-item credit ledger forces a false exclusive choice between them, then records one party as not having done work it demonstrably did. SO SOME OF THE CONFLICT THE COORDINATOR CALLED IRRESOLVABLE IS NOT A CONTRADICTION AT ALL; IT IS THE LEDGER LACKING A WAY TO EXPRESS INDEPENDENT CO-DISCOVERY. That does not rescue per-item attribution - the shared-identity defect stands - but it means the conflicting claims are not evidence that either party is misreporting.

title: Auditing x86 assumptions encoded as numeric literals
description: MEASURED. New FIFTH pattern class, distinct from instances 1-4 which were all #ifdef-greppable. Trigger: import_address() in mm/malloc_wrapper.cc:53 tests *((uint16_t*)imp) == 0x25ff, the x86 encoding of jmp *disp32(%rip), as a bare magic number with NO guard - ungreppable by #ifdef or by any x86 string. Sweep of 938 .c/.cc/.h/.cpp in the sealed pristine winsup tree. CONTROLS FIRST: sensitivity - narrow pattern (pointer deref compared to hex literal) FIRES on the known defect; specificity - only 2 total hits, the other being strfuncs.cc:736 0x8f = JIS-X-0212 lead byte, correctly benign. Broad opcode sweep: 13 raw hits, all triaged. KEY RESULT: path.cc find_fast_cwd_pointer() lines 4846-4965 carries NINE x86-64 byte patterns (0xe8 call rel32 x2, lock btr, mov/lea rip-relative x5, test %rbx REX.W) with ZERO preprocessor directives in 4700-4970 - BUT ITS CALLER find_fast_cwd() IS ARM64-GUARDED AT RUNTIME (path.cc:4975 wincap.host_machine() == IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_ARM64, explicit comment), so it is compiled but NEVER EXECUTED on ARM64 = TRUE NEGATIVE. I corrected my own first reading (unguarded scanner) BEFORE reporting: finding a mechanism is not finding it in play. THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING: the codebase guarded one x86 machine-code scanner for ARM64 and missed the other, and the correct idiom already exists in the same tree. malloc_wrapper.cc has ZERO preprocessor conditionals and NO wincap/host_machine/ARM64/aarch64 reference anywhere (exhaustive scan). Silence explained: the probe sits in __try/__except(NO_ERROR) so faults are swallowed; import_address returns NULL, NULL != &_sigfe_malloc, use_internal=false, every if(!use_internal) forwards to user_data->malloc = itself = unbounded recursion with no diagnostic. Artifact: state/x86-assumptions-as-data-audit.md

title: Closing the getreent link by reading the sealed source
description: MEASURED, narrows the hypothesis to a single arithmetic operation. Sealed winsup/cygwin/include/cygwin/config.h sha 0a664264d08b lines 31 and 36-45: #define __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__ 12800; extern inline struct _reent *__getreent (void) { register char *ret; #ifdef __x86_64__ asm volatile ("movq %gs:8,%0") #else #error unimplemented for this target #endif return (struct _reent *) (ret - __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__); }. THREE RESULTS: (1) %gs:8 IS the TEB StackBase, so the hypothesis targets the right function, and upstream SUBTRACTS __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__ before returning; cygtls.h:304 agrees, _my_tls = *(_cygtls*)((PBYTE)NtCurrentTeb()->Tib.StackBase - __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__). (2) ARITHMETIC CORROBORATED AGAINST AN EARLIER UNRELATED MEASUREMENT: 0x800000000 - 12800 = 0x7FFFFCE00, and my FIRST x86_64 heap dump recorded entry 0x8000050b0 data+0x10 holding exactly 0x7ffffce00 - two independent inputs, same value. (3) THE SEALED PORT HAS NO ARM64 __getreent, only #error unimplemented for this target - FIFTH instance of that family - so the ARM64 implementation is NEW PORT CODE not inherited, satisfying the constraint that the defect must be ARM64-specific in CODE since the StackBase aliasing is architecture-neutral. ONE-READ DISCRIMINATOR REQUIRING NO WATCHPOINT AND NO REBUILD: on ARM64 print the address __getreent()/_my_tls resolves to in the main thread. 0x7FFFFCE00 = correct and exonerates the hypothesis; 0x800000000 = the cygheap base and confirms it, since a store at +8 through that pointer lands on 0x800000008 = cygheap->chain, one 8-byte write, exactly the corrupted slot. NOT ASSERTED: I have not seen the ARM64 __getreent source; established here are the correct semantics, the exact expected value, and a discriminating test. CAUTION RECORDED AND RELAYED: the fixed ARM64 version reads the TEB via x18 and [x18+8] IS StackBase, so a version that correctly reads x18 CAN STILL BE WRONG if it omits the -12800. Getting the TEB register right and the offset arithmetic right are TWO SEPARATE FIXES and only the first is confirmed done - the earlier tpidr_el0 fix may have corrected the register while leaving the arithmetic untouched, which would look like a fix that took while the defect persisted.

title: Confirming the exec signature transfers to the canonical DLL
description: MEASURED, CONFIRMED, TRANSFERS EXACTLY. The coordinator said results pinned to 90bfb483 SHOULD transfer and correctly flagged that as an assumption, so I tested it rather than accepting it. Used the IDENTICAL fixture binary a93e9de9e2af913191ab8b4958edc12df20eec00acd69f54adfd00112c553076, so the DLL was the only variable. Pinned artifact 9fcc134ee26ce3ebc9a359e05eaded2e42cbb6a71e8b6556af8f24dbb658497e, hash-verified on the STAGED COPY before and after. RESULT IDENTICAL TO 90bfb483: direct execl -> child_copy cygheap read copy failed 0x800000000..0x800025780 done 0 Win32 error 6, then couldnt create signal pipe Win32 error 5, execl DOES NOT RETURN; fork+execl -> raw status 0x0b SIGSEGV; cross-fixture p4exec 70e31eee -> same with range ..0x800025810. CONTROLS RE-PASSED AND TWO OF THEM ARE A FUNCTIONAL SOURCE-TO-OBJECT CHECK, which is the coordinator missing-half point answered: a stale object (source says 3 memmove, object has 0) would make the sentinel control FAIL. It passed, so the argv fix is genuinely IN this binary; forkonly PASS likewise confirms the headroom fix is in it. BEHAVIOURAL CONTROLS DETECT STALE-OBJECT MISMATCHES THAT A HASH CHECK CANNOT SEE - the hash proves the binary did not change under me, the controls prove it matches the source I believe produced it.

title: Correcting the revised fork diagnosis third root cause
description: DONE. 68c032ba retracted --disable-dynamicbase cleanly but its REVISION introduced a THIRD wrong root cause and promoted a conditional of mine into a fact. CORRECTED: (1) "struct layout / alignment issue in init_cygheap between architectures" is REFUTED BY THE PROGRAMME OWN DATA - sizeof(init_cygheap) is 0x48A0 on BOTH architectures (I measured 0x48A0 on x86_64 as the lowest chain entry sitting exactly at the struct end; the ARM64 side reports 0x48A0 with offsetof(chain)=8). Same size, same chain offset, so there is no layout divergence. The real reading is that on x86_64 the first chain entry is at the struct end with NO GAP while ARM64 reports it 0x2050 past the end, meaning ~8 KB of allocations exist BELOW the first chain entry and are not on it = ORPHANING by a stray write to cygheap->chain, not a mislaid structure. (2) They stated the wild terminator "traces to CYGHEAP_STORAGE_INITIAL" - I gave that as CONDITIONAL on the captured value being one hex digit wide and explicitly said I had not seen the raw capture. Asked them to hold it as a lead pending width confirmation. (3) The 0x2050 figure is a reported ARM64 number, not my measurement; only the x86_64 baseline is mine. (4) PROCESS: they left fork-diagnosis.md (wrong) beside fork-diagnosis-REVISED.md (right), with the WRONG file holding the more canonical name - the sixth instance of the name-trap family today after gendef2, new-msys-2.0.dll, msys-2.0-ctorfix.dll and the phantom manifest entry. Asked them to correct in place or delete, since a -REVISED suffix relies on the reader noticing a second file exists.

title: Correcting a conditional that outlived its own test
description: DONE. 68c032ba applied my EARLIER instruction and marked the wild-terminator lead CONDITIONAL ("if the width confirms, search narrows; if not, discard"), but our messages crossed: the width had ALREADY been tested and FAILED. Raw bytes 00 A0 2C 00 80 00 00 00 = 0x80002CA000 = 512.0027 GiB AT FULL WIDTH, so the discard branch is the one that fired. Told them to move it from conditional to DISCARDED, noting that leaving it conditional is now WORSE than leaving it a fact, because it reads as open work and the next reader will spend time resolving a condition already resolved against. Also confirmed to them that the ptmalloc/mmap-segment attribution IS consistent with the layout since 0x80002CA000 sits inside MMAP_STORAGE (64 GiB..114,688 GiB), so the original reading stands and my redirect was the error. THEIR POINTS 1, 3 AND 4 WERE CORRECT: no struct-layout claim (sizeof(init_cygheap) identical 0x48A0 both arches, cause is a stray write to cygheap->chain producing orphaned allocations); 0x2050 provenance noted with x86_64 baseline mine and ARM64 0x68F0 theirs; and the duplicate file deleted so a single fork-diagnosis.md carries its own retraction section. NEW LESSON RECORDED: A CONDITIONAL IS ONLY SAFE IF ITS RESOLUTION TRAVELS AS FAST AS THE CONDITION DID. The hedge propagated correctly and then outlived its own test by one message. An unresolved condition sitting in a document is indistinguishable from live work - the mirror image of a conditional decaying into a fact.

title: Correcting my 1<<b entry sizing to bucket_val lookup
description: MEASURED CORRECTION, verified independently against primary source rather than accepted on assertion. Sealed winsup/cygwin/mm/cygheap.cc:281 sha 45737284b0120e55 defines an EXPLICIT LOOKUP TABLE of powers of two AND THEIR MEDIANS: 32,48,64,96,128,192,256,384,512,768,1024,1536,2048,3072,4096,6144,8192,12288,... bucket_val[15]=6144 NOT 32768; 32768 is bucket_val[20]. Line 389 confirms allocation = bucket_val[b] + sizeof(_cmalloc_entry). MY ERROR: I sized entries as 1<<b, so my earlier "needle owned by entry 0x8000050B0" was a FALSE POSITIVE from an inflated extent, and my "all four ARM64 addresses are interior to one 32 KB allocation" was an artefact. Both branches of the decidable fork I posed are dead - ARM64 measured b=15 identical to x86_64 so no size divergence, and with the real table there is no overlap. RE-WALKED x86_64 WITH THE REAL TABLE: 0x8000048a0 b=12 size=2048 data[0x8000048b0..0x8000050b0); 0x8000050b0 b=15 size=6144 data[0x8000050c0..0x8000068c0) contiguous; 0x8000068c0 b=0 size=32 data[0x8000068d0..0x8000068f0) contiguous OWNS THE USERNAME; 0x8000068f0 b=0 size=32 data[0x800006900..0x800006920) contiguous. THREE RESULTS: (1) x86_64 and ARM64 allocation sequences are BYTE-IDENTICAL THROUGH 0x8000068F0 - same addresses, same bucket indices, contiguous to the byte, so the divergence is EXACTLY ONE FIELD; (2) first entry at cygheap+0x48A0 = sizeof(init_cygheap) reconfirmed with correct sizing; (3) ACTIONABLE - on x86_64 the prev of 0x8000068F0 is 0x8000068C0, so THAT is the correct contents of ARM64 slot 0x8000068F8, measured rather than inferred. ERROR CLASS: 1<<b is what most allocators DO, so a plausible convention attracted no scrutiny. A DERIVED NUMBER AGREEING WITH ANOTHER DERIVED NUMBER IS NOT CORROBORATION WHEN BOTH REST ON THE SAME UNSTATED CONVENTION.

title: Correcting the slot conflation - AND WITHDRAWING MY GEOMETRIC EXCLUSION
description: MEASURED CORRECTION, and it exposes an error I propagated. 68c032ba measured directly and 2/2 reproducibly that the cygheap->chain HEAD IS VALID in a running ARM64 process: 43 entries walk clean and the wild prev appears at entry 0x8000068F0. TWO DIFFERENT SLOTS HAVE BEEN CONFLATED ALL THREAD, BY ME AND BY THE COORDINATOR: cygheap->chain = cygheap+8 = 0x800000008, whereas prev of entry 0x8000068F0 = entry+8 = 0x8000068F8; DIFFERENCE 0x68F0 = 26,864 bytes. THE CORRUPTED SLOT IS 0x8000068F8, THE PREV FIELD OF THE 44TH ENTRY, NOT cygheap->chain. A watchpoint armed on 0x800000008 will not fire - that is 68c032ba point 3 and it is correct. SECOND CONSEQUENCE: this kills the StackBase hypothesis INDEPENDENTLY. The entire appeal of StackBase+8 was that it lands on 0x800000008, but the corruption is at 0x8000068F8, so even if __getreent had returned the raw StackBase it would have clobbered the HEAD not the 44th entry prev. THAT HYPOTHESIS WAS NEVER GEOMETRICALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE OBSERVED SITE AND I RELAYED IT WITHOUT CHECKING THAT - the StackBase measurement I supplied was sound, but I did not test whether the mechanism reached the place the damage actually is. THIRD: their finding that the wild value is ASLR-RANDOMISED and changes every run VINDICATES MY CYGHEAP_STORAGE_INITIAL RETRACTION for a second independent reason - a per-run varying value cannot be a named constant. SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the correct contents of 0x8000068F8 is 0x8000068C0, measured twice from raw bytes on healthy x86_64; prev sits at +8 and survives free so it is immune to every allocator subtlety argued today, and it is the success criterion for any instrumentation. CAUTION RAISED ON THE SOLE SURVIVING CANDIDATE: THREAD_STORAGE_HIGH and CYGHEAP_STORAGE_LOW are the same address, so the cygheap sits immediately above a region the OS also allocates into; a stray OS write at cygheap+0x68F8 needs a named mechanism just as much as one at cygheap+8 did. OS loader during lazy DLL load is a CANDIDATE, not a mechanism. || WITHDRAWN 2026-09-03 11:36, MY FIFTH DISTINCT FAILURE MODE TODAY AND THE MOST DANGEROUS. 68c032ba reconciled the two observations: chain head wild during startup, valid post-init, corruption baked into the entry AT BIRTH. Verified verbatim against sealed mm/cygheap.cc lines 396-398: rvc->b = b; rvc->prev = cygheap->chain; cygheap->chain = rvc. SO rvc->prev IS A COPY OF cygheap->chain TAKEN AT ALLOCATION TIME, and an entry BORN with a wild prev PROVES cygheap->chain WAS WILD AT THAT INSTANT; the head then heals as later allocations prepend. THEREFORE 0x8000068F8 IS WHERE THE EVIDENCE WAS PRESERVED, NOT WHERE THE STORE LANDED - THE STORE LANDED ON cygheap->chain = 0x800000008. MY ARGUMENT THAT A HEAD-WRITE WOULD HAVE CLOBBERED THE HEAD RATHER THAN THE 44TH ENTRY PREV, AND THEREFORE EXCLUDED HEAD-WRITING MECHANISMS, IS BACKWARDS: a transient head write is EXACTLY what produces this signature, and anyone applying my exclusion would rule out the true cause. Asked both 68c032ba and the coordinator to strike it. WHAT CHANGES: __getreent stays eliminated but ON THE MEASUREMENT GROUND ONLY (their one-read test); my geometric ground is withdrawn. 0x800000008 is BACK as the write target, transiently during startup - reinforcing their point 4 that the watchpoint must be armed DURING STARTUP before the LOAD_DLL burst, not on a running process. The expected value 0x8000068C0 gains meaning: it is what cygheap->chain SHOULD have contained when 0x8000068F0 was allocated, and since 0x8000068C0 is the immediately preceding entry the window is between TWO ADJACENT _cmalloc CALLS. c63ab774 new datum tightens it: fetch_account_from_windows never fires before the wild birth, so the five token-driven DLL loads are AFTER the store and the window is EARLIER than the loader hypothesis assumed. FAILURE MODE, REUSABLE: I TREATED THE LOCATION OF THE EVIDENCE AS THE LOCATION OF THE WRITE. In a linked list a corrupt value propagates forward into a preserved copy while the original slot heals, so visible damage and impact site are DIFFERENT ADDRESSES. Shares its shape with the w-ctorfix and --disable-dynamicbase episodes: a confident structural claim, locally coherent, propagated before being tested against the thing it was meant to explain. Caught not by review of my reasoning but by another session reconciling two observations I had treated as contradictory.

title: Correcting my own requested-versus-observed overclaim
description: ACCEPTED AND CORRECTED IN THE SEALED ARTIFACT. I phrased the surviving fact as "a handle DUPLICATED bInheritHandle=TRUE". THAT IS AN API REQUEST, NOT AN OBSERVED STATE. DuplicateHandle is CALLED with TRUE - verified in source at sigproc.cc:938 - but nobody had measured GetHandleInformation(parent) at the CreateProcessW instant, so the flag actual state was NOT established. THIS IS EXACTLY MY OWN ERROR CLASS AND I LET IT THROUGH: I have spent the session insisting on measured-versus-assumed and then allowed a requested value to stand as an observed one, in a sentence headed for a bug filing. Corrected the artifact to "a handle FOR WHICH bInheritHandle=TRUE WAS REQUESTED", with the missing measurement named inline. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND PEDANTRY, and the coordinator framing is right: an overstated premise is the fastest way to have an entire bug report dismissed - the same failure the DYNAMIC_BASE note was corrected for. Both outcomes of the real check beat filing without it: bit CLEAR names the root cause as ours; bit SET upgrades the report from "we assume, because we asked" to "we verified at the instant of the call".

title: Recording that native make ships as mingw32-make.exe not make.exe

Any build script invoking bare "make" will fail unless aliased. Also: libtool 2.6.2-1 ships ZERO exes (shell scripts only, unusable without a shell); texinfo makeinfo/texi2any are scripts.

title: Cross-checking ARM64 clobber addresses against my x86_64 measurement
description: MEASURED cross-check, yields a decidable fork. c63ab774 narrowed the clobber to a single 8-byte store between two adjacent _cmalloc calls, with the ARM64 username entry at 0x8000068C0 correctly chained to 0x8000050B0 and the very next entry at 0x8000068F0 born wild. I ALREADY MEASURED 0x8000050B0 ON x86_64: it is a live chain entry with b=15, size 1<<15 = 32,768 bytes, data spanning [0x8000050C0 .. 0x80000D0C0). ALL FOUR ARM64 ADDRESSES ARE INTERIOR TO THAT SINGLE x86_64 ALLOCATION: 0x8000068C0 = data+0x1800, 0x8000068D0 = data+0x1810, 0x8000068E0 = data+0x1820 (exactly where I found the username string on x86_64), 0x8000068F0 = data+0x1830. SO THE SAME ADDRESS 0x8000050B0 IS A LIVE CHAIN ENTRY ON BOTH ARCHITECTURES, which implies the early allocation sequence is deterministic and identical up to that point and the divergence begins after it. DECIDABLE FORK, one read settles it: what is b for the entry at 0x8000050B0 on ARM64? (a) If small, the same allocation slot got a radically different size than x86_64 b=15, pointing at a SIZE COMPUTATION rather than a stray store. (b) If also 15, then the ARM64 chain holds entries at 0x8000068C0 and 0x8000068F0 lying INSIDE the data of 0x8000050B0 - a self-overlapping chain, a worse finding, and one that would mean the corruption PREDATES the born-wild entry. SELF-CONSISTENCY CHECK PASSES on their reading: 0x8000068F0 - 0x8000068C0 = 0x30 = 16-byte header + 32-byte data, implying bucket b=5, and crutkasLocal is 13 bytes incl NUL which is exactly bucket 5.

title: Eliminating the explicit inherit-handle-list hypothesis
description: ELIMINATED FROM SOURCE BEFORE I PROPOSED IT, which is the only reason it is not a tenth error. The signature - handle marked inheritable, CreateProcessW passed bInheritHandles=TRUE, correct numeric value transmitted, yet ABSENT from the childs handle table - is exactly what STARTUPINFOEX with PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST produces: when an explicit handle list is supplied, ONLY handles on that list are inherited, and everything else is excluded despite bInheritHandles=TRUE and the inherit flag being set. MEASURED: NEITHER PATH USES IT. Tree-wide sweep for STARTUPINFOEX, EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT, PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, UpdateProcThreadAttribute, InitializeProcThreadAttributeList and lpAttributeList returns hits ONLY in fhandler/pty.cc (lines 237-3793), which is a different path entirely. spawn.cc:340 uses a plain STARTUPINFOW si = {} with si.cb = sizeof (si) at spawn.cc:624, and fork.cc:321 the same with fork.cc:324 - NEITHER sets EXTENDED_STARTUPINFO_PRESENT in c_flags. HYPOTHESIS DEAD. NOTED IN PASSING, NOT PURSUED: both paths set si.cbReserved2 (spawn.cc:557 sizeof(*this), fork.cc:327 sizeof(ch)), the classic lpReserved2 channel by which the child_info block itself is handed to the child - so the STRUCT travels as DATA and only the HANDLE VALUE inside it depends on real inheritance. That distinction matters for anyone reasoning about this and I am recording it as an observation, not a lead.

title: Escalating a third re-derivation of the harmful dynamicbase change
description: ESCALATED. 68c032ba reported receiving a DIRECTION pointing back at the retracted --disable-dynamicbase hypothesis, citing its OWN original addresses 0x7ffdac3c0000 / 0x7ffdb10b0000 / 0x7ffdae6f0000 back at it as evidence for ASLR causation. This did NOT come from my relay, which carried the coordinator block saying the opposite. So a THIRD source re-asserted the harmful change AFTER two retractions. THIRD INDEPENDENT DERIVATION. Asked 68c032ba to name the source. RAISED WITH COORDINATOR: the retraction is losing the race against the inference, so putting the measurement adjacent to the link line in Makefile.am should be prioritised - anyone reading DllCharacteristics 0x0160 plus a randomised-looking base will keep arriving at the same conclusion, and conversation-resident corrections do not reach them. THE GOOD PART: 68c032ba HELD ITS GROUND against a directive using evidence, despite having already been corrected twice by me and having every social reason to comply. It checked the new instruction against measurements and refused. Told it so explicitly and asked it to keep doing that including against me. PROCESS COST PATTERN NOW VISIBLE: work is directed to sessions the coordinator cannot see, those sessions reason correctly from what they are given, and the only thing catching it is a session that happens to hold a contradicting measurement - that is LUCK, NOT ARCHITECTURE. Proposed two fixes: measurement living in the tree at the point of inference, and a single named owner per hypothesis so re-proposals reach someone who knows it was already tested.

title: Recording a fifth misattribution and its independence cost
description: ESCALATED. 68c032ba credited me with a 4/4 TEB identity confirmation across ASLR-randomised TEBs, a search finding 481 str xM,[xN,#8] sites, and a caveat about MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION layout. I DID NONE OF IT. My last cygheap message was 11:43 stating I had nothing further unless a measurement contradicted something I supplied. Almost certainly 290c9aaf, the context running under my project identity. FIFTH SUCH EPISODE. STANDING CAVEAT UNCHANGED: I cannot prove my identity did not produce it. THE SPECIFIC COST THIS TIME IS INDEPENDENCE, NOT JUST CREDIT: 68c032ba wrote that my 4/4 "closes any remaining doubt" about c63ab774 independent measurement - but IF BOTH RESULTS CAME FROM THE SAME PLACE THEY ARE NOT INDEPENDENT AND THE DOUBT IS NOT CLOSED. That distinction is the entire value of a second source, and misattribution destroys it silently. Asked for correct attribution on that basis rather than on ownership.

title: Closing ASLR flag - no regression, DYNAMIC_BASE is mandatory
description: RESOLVED AND INVERTED. --disable-dynamicbase was retracted as a NON-FIX; Windows-on-ARM MANDATES ASLR. Independently reproduced by me on this ARM64 host over 6 stock ARM64 system DLLs (version, winmm, bcrypt, wintrust, cryptbase, profapi; all Machine=0xaa64) with four controls: A pristine copy LOADED 6/6 (harness positive control); B byte-identical rewrite LOADED 6/6 (rewrite pipeline not the variable); C DYNAMIC_BASE bit 0x0040 cleared FAILED err=193 ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT 6/6; D C plus checksum zeroed FAILED err=193 6/6 (not a checksum artefact); E HIGH_ENTROPY_VA 0x0020 cleared alone LOADED 5/6. REFINEMENT BEYOND THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: only DYNAMIC_BASE is mandated, HIGH_ENTROPY_VA is NOT. bcrypt E returns 577 ERROR_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH = signature enforcement, not an ASLR counterexample; note 193 fires BEFORE signature validation on C/D. CONCLUSION: DllCharacteristics 0x0160 on msys-2.0-ctorfix.dll is CORRECT AND REQUIRED; msys-2.0-fixedbase.dll at 0x0100 is UNLOADABLE BY CONSTRUCTION and was a control proving a platform rule, not a fix. My filename-inferred regression flag is withdrawn - and had I claimed it, it would have sent someone to restore a change that makes the image unloadable.

title: Flagging that the build driver make is not from the WoA GCC chain

title: Recording the struct-packing harness bug that would have blocked release
description: MEASURED self-catch, FOURTH of the day. My first tree audit reported "files with NumberOfLinks>1: 158 - HARDLINKS PRESENT", a RELEASE-BLOCKING claim asserting NO_INSTALL_HARDLINKS=1 had failed and the package would ship a fraction of its files. IT WAS WRONG AND IT WAS MINE: BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION packs FILETIME on 4-byte alignment, but C# LayoutKind.Sequential default padded the long fields to 8, so every field after dwFileAttributes was read at the wrong offset. TWO THINGS EXPOSED IT BEFORE IT LEFT THE THREAD: (1) the values were IMPOSSIBLE - link counts of 131072/196608/262144/327680/786432, when link counts are small integers; (2) TWO FIELDS FROM THE SAME STRUCT CONTRADICTED EACH OTHER - 158 multilink files alongside 158 distinct file indexes with 0 shared. A struct that disagrees with itself is misaligned, not reporting a finding. title: ELIMINATED - cygtls does NOT overflow the pad
description: HYPOTHESIS WITH A ONE-NUMBER TEST, EXPLICITLY NOT ASSERTED. Prompted by 68c032ba distinction that the StackBase+8 MECHANISM is geometrically sound and only the __getreent CANDIDATE is dead. MEASURED: _my_tls is referenced 275 times across 47 files in the sealed tree, and cygtls.h:304 defines it as *(_cygtls*)((PBYTE)NtCurrentTeb()->Tib.StackBase - __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__) - THE SAME ARITHMETIC __getreent USES - so eliminating __getreent eliminates one consumer out of ~275. MEASURED: _cygtls mandates struct _reent local_clib AT OFFSET 0. MEASURED GEOMETRY from my own StackBase measurement: main-thread _my_tls base = 0x800000000 - 12800 = 0x7FFFFCE00, occupying [0x7FFFFCE00, 0x800000000) exactly 12,800 bytes, SO ITS UPPER BOUND IS EXACTLY THE CYGHEAP BASE. DERIVED: _cygtls offset 12800 -> cygheap+0; OFFSET 12808 -> cygheap+8 = cygheap->chain; offset 12816 -> cygheap+0x10. HYPOTHESIS: if sizeof(_cygtls) exceeds __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__ on ARM64, _my_tls writes overflow into the cygheap and a field at offset 12808 hits cygheap->chain exactly. WHY IT WOULD FIT: _cygtls embeds struct _reent, sigset_t, siginfo_t, stack_t and saved-context state, ALL ARCHITECTURE-DEPENDENT SIZES, so a struct fitting 12,800 bytes on x86_64 need not on ARM64; TLS is written from the earliest moments of startup, matching c63ab774 finding that the window is EARLIER than the loader hypothesis assumed; a pointer/HANDLE field would look page-aligned, OS-heap shaped and ASLR-varying, matching 68c032ba finding 2; and it is one 8-byte store. KEY SUPPORTING MEASUREMENT EXPLAINING THE SILENCE: THERE IS NO static_assert ANYWHERE IN THE TREE THAT sizeof(_cygtls) <= __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__, despite the codebase using static_assert freely in errmap.h x5, dlfcn.cc, errno.cc, dev_disk.cc, call_once.c and tss.c. cygtls.cc:24 merely declares char buf[__CYGTLS_PADSIZE__]. So if the struct outgrew the pad on ARM64 NOTHING AT BUILD TIME WOULD SAY SO. TEST: print sizeof(_cygtls) on ARM64 and compare with 12800. NOT PURSUED BUT NOTED: create_posix_thread.cc:85 is x86_64 INLINE ASM (subq %[CYGTLS], %%rsp), another x86-only construct needing an ARM64 equivalent; and Makefile.am:422 generates TLS offsets from cygtls.h via the gawk script scripts/gentls_offsets, worth checking for architecture handling. LABELLING: NOT ESTABLISHED that sizeof(_cygtls) exceeds 12800 on ARM64. Flagged to the recipient that I have been wrong five times today and this is exactly the shape of claim that got me each time - a coherent structural story offered before the one number that tests it. || ELIMINATED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-03 11:43. c63ab774 printed the number: sizeof(_cygtls) = 5016, __CYGTLS_PADSIZE__ = 12800, HEADROOM 7784 BYTES. THE ANTECEDENT IS FALSE - no overflow occurs and the hypothesis is dead. OUTCOME ASSESSMENT: this is the system working. The hypothesis was labelled untested, shipped WITH its own one-number falsifier, and was killed by that test within minutes - a hypothesis that names its own falsifier and dies fast costs almost nothing. STRONGER CONSEQUENCE DERIVED FROM THEIR NUMBER PLUS MY MEASURED GEOMETRY: with 7784 bytes of headroom, the ENTIRE _cygtls/TEB FAMILY IS NOW GEOMETRICALLY EXCLUDED, not merely this hypothesis. Any _my_tls-based write - even one with wrong FIELD offsets - stays inside the pad and cannot reach cygheap+8. Only a write with a WRONG BASE could, and the base is proven correct by the __getreent one-read measurement. So the remaining candidates must write to cygheap+8 via a base that is not StackBase-derived at all. That is a BOUND ON THE REMAINING SEARCH SPACE, not a new hypothesis - deliberately not proposing a replacement mechanism, since generating a replacement cause inside the acknowledgement of a dead one is the retraction-is-not-self-limiting failure I catalogued earlier today.

title: Identifying the allocation born wild on ARM64
description: MEASURED from raw bytes on healthy x86_64 (Git for Windows msys-2.0.dll 3.6.9, sleep.exe, external ReadProcessMemory). RAW WINDOW at 0x8000068c0: header b/ptr=0 prev=0x8000050b0; data 0x8000068d0 = 01 00 00 00 then "crutkasLocal" at 0x8000068e0. Header at 0x8000068f0: b/ptr=0, PREV = c0 68 00 00 08 00 00 00 = 0x8000068C0 READ DIRECTLY FROM RAW BYTES, independent of my walker - this is the value the ARM64 slot 0x8000068F8 should hold, and it is the number the whole hunt turns on. DATA from 0x800006900: 03 00 00 00 then a UTF-16 NT PATH at 0x800006910 = "\\??\\C:\\Program Files\\Git\\var\\run\\cygfork", 40 chars, running to 0x800006960. SO THE ALLOCATION IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE USERNAME cstrdup - THE ONE BORN WILD ON ARM64 - IS A FORK-MACHINERY PATH ALLOCATION. Measured in a plain sleep.exe that never forks, consistent with the corruption being present in never-forking processes since the path is built at startup regardless. NARROWS the live question "what in user.init()/setup_cygheap receives an OS-allocated pointer and stores it" to whatever composes /var/run/cygfork as an NT path during cygheap setup; cygheap.cc has installation_root_buf at ~line 269 immediately above the bucket_val table. UNRESOLVED AND DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: the header reads b=0 which by bucket_val[0] means a 32-byte block ending at 0x800006920, YET THE PATH RUNS TO 0x800006960. Those do not reconcile. Could be a length-prefixed structure whose buffer extends beyond the block, or a b field I am still misreading. After three structure errors today I reported the bytes and the inconsistency rather than inventing a fourth account. Both headline results are direct byte reads and do not depend on resolving it. WARNING PASSED ON: if that allocation is larger than 32 bytes, entry spacing around it is not what a naive walk assumes.
