title: Measuring whether DLL ASLR randomises per process or per boot
description: MEASURED, DECISIVE. Triggered because session 68c032ba independently re-derived -Wl,--disable-dynamicbase as the fork fix, premised on "the child gets a different base than the parent". MY FIRST TEST HAD NO SENSITIVITY AND WAS DISCARDED: I used Git for Windows msys-2.0.dll and saw one identical base across 4 concurrent processes, but that DLL carries DllCharacteristics=0x0000 with ASLR DISABLED, so the result said nothing about ASLR. Re-ran with a copy of a stock ARM64 DLL carrying DllCharacteristics=0x4160 (DYNAMIC_BASE SET): 5 concurrent processes all at base 0x7ffe4ed60000, and 3 sequential loads after full unload also 0x7ffe4ed60000; DISTINCT BASES = 1. Critically 0x7ffe4ed60000 is NOT the preferred base, so the image WAS relocated and ASLR is demonstrably active, yet every process got the same address. CONCLUSION: Windows randomises a given image ONCE PER BOOT, NOT PER PROCESS. Therefore parent and child receive the SAME base; fork needs "same base in parent and child", not "fixed base", and ASLR satisfies it. Combined with the six-DLL err 193 result, --disable-dynamicbase is BOTH premised on a false mechanism AND actively harmful.

title: Measuring whether the correct-value-but-err6 signature has a plain Win32 cause
description: MEASURED IN PURE WIN32 ON ARM64, WITH CONTROLS. Motivated by the narrowed exec signature: handle duplicated bInheritHandle=TRUE, minted in the very process calling CreateProcessW, that call passing bInheritHandles=TRUE, child receives the CORRECT NUMERIC VALUE, handle ABSENT from the childs table with err 6. LOAD-BEARING STRUCTURAL FACT I NOTED FROM SOURCE: both paths set si.cbReserved2 (spawn.cc:557, fork.cc:327), the lpReserved2 channel that hands the child_info block to the child - SO THE STRUCT TRAVELS AS DATA AND ONLY THE HANDLE VALUE INSIDE IT DEPENDS ON REAL INHERITANCE. Value transmission and handle transmission are DECOUPLED, which is what makes "correct value, invalid handle" possible at all. THREE-GENERATION PROBE, gen0 signals slot2, values passed down as command-line data. ARM A gen0->gen1 inherit, gen1->gen2 inherit: GEN2 sees slot2 SIGNALLED, TRACKING gen0 choice, all four valid at identical values - SO HANDLE INHERITANCE IS TRANSITIVE and "inheritance does not survive a generation" is REFUTED. ARM B gen0->gen1 inherit, gen1->gen2 NO-inherit: GEN1 correct and tracking, GEN2 slot2 INVALID err6 WHILE THE VALUE 0x340 ARRIVED INTACT AS DATA - THE EXACT SIGNATURE REPRODUCED. ARM C gen0->gen1 no-inherit negative control: GEN1 already broken with err6 plus noise, detector confirmed. INCIDENTAL: arm B slot3 read VALID+SIGNALLED though it was NOT the signalled object - another adjacent-slot false positive, reinforcing identity-not-validity. WHAT IT IMPLIES, AS A QUESTION NOT A CLAIM: the signature is produced by ANY BREAK IN THE INHERITANCE CHAIN BETWEEN THE MINTING PROCESS AND THE READING PROCESS, so the question is whether the process that READS child_info->parent is the same process created by THAT CreateProcessW call or is a generation removed. EXPLICITLY NOT A CLAIM ABOUT THE CYGWIN EXEC PATH - I have had THREE hypotheses die in this sub-area tonight (inheritance-clearing gated behind !iscygwin(), the storage-class lifetime inference, and the explicit handle-list), so this is offered as a measured mechanism class plus the question it raises, for the tree owner to accept or discard.

title: Measuring handle identity versus validity with full controls
description: MEASURED, DECISIVE, AND IT UNDERMINES THE EXEC +8/+12 FINDING. Purpose-built minimal probe on ARM64: no MSYS2, no Cygwin, no fixture, no debugger. Parent creates 4 inheritable manual-reset events, signals EXACTLY ONE, passes the 4 handle VALUES to a CreateProcessW child; child reports GetHandleInformation (validity) and WaitForSingleObject(h,0) (state). IDENTITY asserted only if the slot the child reports signalled TRACKS the slot the parent chose, across more than one choice. ARM A inherit=YES signal=slot0 -> slot0 SIGNALLED rest notsig. ARM B inherit=YES signal=slot2 -> slot2 SIGNALLED, THE ANSWER MOVED = specificity established. ARM C inherit=YES signal=NONE -> all valid none signalled, rules out an always-signalled detector. ARM D NEGATIVE CONTROL inherit=NO signal=slot0 -> slot0 notsig BUT slot1 VALID+SIGNALLED, slot2 err5 ACCESS_DENIED, slot3 INVALID err6. SO WITH INHERITANCE FULLY OFF THE CHILD STILL REPORTED A VALID+SIGNALLED HANDLE AT AN ADJACENT VALUE. ARM E, the delta scenario measured directly, parent signalled slot0 every time, child probed at true value plus shift: shift -12 gave TWO false positives (slot1 and slot3 VALID+SIGNALLED); -8 slot2 SIGNALLED; -4 slot2 SIGNALLED; +4 none; +8 slot2 SIGNALLED; +12 slot1 SIGNALLED. IN 5 OF 6 ARMS A SHIFTED PROBE REPORTED VALID+SIGNALLED AND IN NONE WAS IT THE OBJECT THE PARENT SIGNALLED - EVERY ONE A FALSE POSITIVE. CONCLUSION: an observation of "a valid parent handle at recorded-8/-12" is FULLY REPRODUCIBLE BY COINCIDENCE and CANNOT support an identity claim. NOT ESTABLISHED EITHER WAY: this does NOT refute the exec defect, it refutes the INFERENCE from validity to identity. STRUCTURAL REASON: handle values allocate densely in a low range (observed 0x338-0x374) at 4-byte granularity and the child OWN table populates the same range, so a +/-4/8/12 probe lands on a real handle with high probability. THE DISCRIMINATOR THAT WORKS: signal a chosen object and require the child to report THAT slot, across at least two different choices. Supersedes my earlier no-negative-control probe.

title: Handle-value preservation CONFIRMED by identity - but my original evidence was invalid
description: MEASURED, REFUTES A PROPAGATING PREMISE. The coordinator stated to the heartbeat context: "WINDOWS DOES NOT DOCUMENT A GUARANTEE THAT INHERITED HANDLE VALUES ARE PRESERVED - the kernel assigns slots in the new process. Fork child is a near-clone with an identical handle-allocation history so slots coincide; the exec child is a different image with a different history, so they need not." It was correctly labelled as a reason-for-the-control rather than a mechanism, but the entire two-outcomes-two-hunts branch analysis rests on it. PURPOSE-BUILT PROBE, independent of the heartbeat fixture, harness and debugger: parent creates 4 inheritable events via CreateEventW with bInheritHandle=1, records their values, then calls CreateProcessW with bInheritHandles=TRUE twice - CASE A spawning the SAME image (fork-analogue) and CASE B spawning a GENUINELY DIFFERENT image (other.exe, 4608 B vs hprobe.exe 6656 B, different code and different PE). Child calls GetHandleInformation on each numeric value. RESULT: parent values 0x348 0x34c 0x350 0x354; CASE A 4/4 VALID; CASE B 4/4 VALID. SO WINDOWS DOES PRESERVE INHERITED HANDLE VALUES, INCLUDING TO A DIFFERENT IMAGE, AND THE different-image-means-different-slots REASONING IS FALSE. Measured on THIS ARM64 host with native ARM64 processes, so preservation holds on the architecture where the defect is claimed. Consistent with documented Windows behaviour that an inherited handle has the same value and access rights as the original. BOUNDED OBSERVATION, NOT A MECHANISM: Windows handle values are multiples of 4, so the reported deltas of +8 and +12 correspond to exactly 2 and 3 handle slots, and the recorded value is always HIGHER than the received one. SCOPE LIMIT STATED: this establishes the OS-LEVEL guarantee for direct CreateProcess handle inheritance. It does NOT establish anything about Cygwin exec specific transfer path, which may pass handles by other means. I deliberately propose no cause - supervisor has stopped hypothesis generation, and my record today is 5 proposed mechanisms all refuted versus measurements and eliminations that all held. || SELF-CAUGHT 2026-09-03 22:17, EVIDENTIAL BASIS CORRECTED. I ran the two controls my first probe lacked: an INHERITANCE-OFF negative control, and an IDENTITY check (parent signals exactly one event; child reports which value is signalled, proving same kernel object rather than mere validity). RESULT, parent handles 0x344 0x348 0x34c 0x350 with ONLY index 2 signalled: NEGATIVE CONTROL bInheritHandles=FALSE, different image -> 4/4 VALID, signalled index 1, IDENTITY NOT PROVEN. TEST bInheritHandles=TRUE, different image -> 4/4 VALID, signalled index 2, MATCHES PARENT, IDENTITY PROVEN. SO MY ORIGINAL METRIC HAD NO SPECIFICITY: "4/4 parent handle values are valid in the child" IS RETURNED IDENTICALLY WITH INHERITANCE OFF, because a fresh process allocates its own handles into those same low slots - in the NEG arm one of the child OWN objects was even signalled at 0x348, exactly the coincidence that makes validity meaningless. This is the same failure class I catalogued in others: a detector that returns the same answer in both arms. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND IS NOW PROPERLY EVIDENCED: Windows DOES preserve inherited handle values across CreateProcess including into a genuinely different image, proven by IDENTITY (signalled index matches) rather than by validity. Measured on this ARM64 host with native ARM64 processes. IMPORTANT FOR ANYONE RE-RUNNING IT: the original probe design would show 4/4 in both arms and correctly prove nothing; only the identity marker discriminates. DIRECTLY APPLICABLE MEASUREMENT SUGGESTION PASSED ON, not a mechanism: anyone comparing handle VALUES across exec should verify SAME KERNEL OBJECT via a signalled-state or object-identity marker, since validity alone does not distinguish an inherited handle from a coincidental one at the same slot.

title: Measuring whether main-thread StackBase aliases cygheap chain
description: MEASURED, PRECONDITION CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Hypothesis reached me second-hand, attributed to me in error, originating in the 290c9aaf supervisor context: that __getreent() reads StackBase from the TEB and something dereferences StackBase+8, landing on cygheap->chain. I TESTED IT rather than dismiss it for provenance. Read NT_TIB.StackBase at TEB+8 for every thread of live MSYS2 processes (sleep.exe and bash.exe, x86_64 Git for Windows) via NtQueryInformationThread + ReadProcessMemory. RESULT: THE MAIN THREAD StackBase IS EXACTLY 0x800000000, the cygheap base, on BOTH programs; all other threads have ordinary low stacks (0x11050000, 0x11330000, 0x11880000, ...). This follows directly from the sealed memory_layout.h constants I measured earlier: THREAD_STORAGE_HIGH = 0x800000000 and CYGHEAP_STORAGE_LOW = 0x800000000 ARE THE SAME ADDRESS, so the regions abut; stacks grow down, so the main thread StackBase sits at the top of THREAD_STORAGE, byte-identical to the cygheap base. THEREFORE StackBase+8 ALIASES cygheap->chain PRECISELY, which would explain a single 8-byte store landing exactly where the corruption is. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT THAT PREVENTS A FOURTH DEAD END: I measured this ON x86_64 WHERE FORK WORKS, so the aliasing is ARCHITECTURE-NEUTRAL. The hypothesis therefore CANNOT be "the layout differs on ARM64" - it requires an ARM64-SPECIFIC DIFFERENCE IN THE CODE performing the arithmetic, i.e. that ARM64 __getreent() dereferences the raw StackBase where x86_64 does not. LABELLING: measured = the StackBase values and layout constants; derived = that StackBase+8 aliases chain, arithmetic on measured values; NOT ESTABLISHED BY ME = that ARM64 __getreent() does that arithmetic, since I have not seen that code, and that is the link which decides the hypothesis.

title: MY TENTH ERROR - I eliminated the true root cause by inspection
description: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL ERROR I MADE, AND IT DESERVES TO BE RECORDED PLAINLY. I wrote, as a measured-sounding elimination: "NOT inheritance-clearing. SetHandleInformation (parent, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, 0) at spawn.cc:597 sits inside if (!iscygwin()) at spawn.cc:594 - NOT TAKEN when exec-ing a Cygwin program, which is this case." THAT WAS THE TRUE CAUSE AND I RULED IT OUT. I even flagged at the time that I had formed the hypothesis from a grep hit and then refuted it by reading the block - and I took that as evidence of rigour when it was the opposite: I read the CONTROL FLOW correctly and then evaluated the PREDICATE BY ITS MEANING RATHER THAN ITS VALUE. I asked what iscygwin() SHOULD return for a Cygwin target and never asked what it DOES return on ARM64. A ONE-LINE INSTRUMENTATION WOULD HAVE SETTLED IT AND I DID NOT RUN ONE BECAUSE I BELIEVED I HAD ALREADY SETTLED IT BY READING. GENERALISATION, sharpened by c63ab774: AN ACCURATELY-NAMED PREDICATE RETURNING A WRONG VALUE IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN A MISLEADINGLY-NAMED ONE, BECAUSE NOTHING ABOUT IT LOOKS SUSPICIOUS. iscygwin() really does mean "is the target a Cygwin exec"; it was simply computing the wrong answer. This is a new variant of the name-versus-content family - the previous eight instances tonight all involved FILES; this one is a FUNCTION. MY OWN RULE ALREADY COVERED IT AND I DID NOT APPLY IT: "any instrument used to prove absence must first be shown to detect a known positive" - I used READING as the instrument to prove an absence and never validated that the instrument could see the positive. THE COST: a confident elimination removed the correct answer from consideration for several cycles across multiple sessions.

title: Observing a byte-identical DLL across an mtime advance

During my exec run the DLL /root/xc/w-link/bld/winsup/cygwin/new-msys-2.0.dll advanced its mtime from 2026-09-03 22:44:52.324128114 to 22:59:38.430487751 while its sha256 remained EXACTLY 90bfb483ae44aea20f3f9491bd42d92b1c3233cdf1b35fac580f9791d4dea310 and its size remained 30897141 B. title: Measuring the blast radius of the ARM64 iscygwin misclassification
description: MEASURED, AND IT MATTERS FOR THE FILING AND FOR REGRESSION SCOPE. iscygwin() has SEVENTEEN call sites: spawn.cc 12, sigproc.cc 3, exceptions.cc 2. THE HANDLE STRIP WAS ONE OF SEVENTEEN DECISIONS BEING TAKEN ON A WRONG ANSWER on ARM64. Others that were silently on the non-Cygwin branch all along include spawn.cc:882 synced = iscygwin() ? sync (pi.dwProcessId, pi.hProcess, INFINITE) : true - PARENT/CHILD SYNC SKIPPED; spawn.cc:900 close_all_files (iscygwin()); spawn.cc:754 !iscygwin() && mode == _P_OVERLAY; spawn.cc:771 iscygwin() && !(c_flags & CREATE_SUSPENDED); sigproc.cc:1204 !iscygwin() && (exit_code & 0xffff0000) != 0xc0000000 - EXIT CODE TRANSLATION; sigproc.cc:1044 and 1071; exceptions.cc:1022 and 1673 - SIGNAL HANDLING AFTER EXEC. title: Re-characterising exec from zero against the fork-fixed DLL
description: IN PROGRESS. Coordinator assigned as the programme critical path. CLEAN SHEET - ALL PRIOR EXEC WORK IS VOID AND MUST NOT BE USED AS A STARTING POINT. Reason it is void: the nine prior eliminations were all measured against a failure mode that NO LONGER OCCURS. Separately my own identity probe already removed the +8/+12 handle-delta fingerprint the last characterisation rested on. CONSTRAINTS: (1) CHARACTERISE, DO NOT PATCH - c63ab774 owns every edit to the runtime tree. (2) Test ONLY against DLL sha256 90bfb483ae44aea20f3f9491bd42d92b1c3233cdf1b35fac580f9791d4dea310, which carries BOTH fixes (the _dll_crt0 stack subtraction and the two memmove sites); DO NOT test against 54e464d0 or 20ad86ba. (3) VERIFY THE DLL HASH BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT - my own standing rule that every claim names the exact sha256. (4) strlen IS NOT A VALIDITY CHECK on this platform: pre-fix, a 24-char argv came back with two chars dropped and two doubled at UNCHANGED length 24, so compare BYTE-FOR-BYTE; corruption position tracked total command-line length so a handful of probes can all miss. (5) Every instrument must be shown to detect a known positive before any absence is claimed.  ||  COMPLETED. See exec-recharacterisation-90bfb483.md. HEADLINE: fork WORKS 3/3 and exec FAILS, on the same hash-verified DLL, same harness, same fixture. Failure is child_copy cygheap read, 0x800000000..0x800025780, done 0, Win32 error 6 (ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE), then fatal error couldnt create signal pipe Win32 error 5. execl DOES NOT RETURN. fork+exec child KILLED BY SIGNAL 11 (raw status 0x0b). REPRODUCED WITH THEIR p4exec.exe sha 70e31eee against the same DLL so not an artefact of my nostdlib link. THREE BRIEFED CLAIMS REFUTED: child_copy/Win32 error 6 are NOT gone; execl does NOT return; the child is NOT exiting 99 but dying of SIGSEGV. INSTRUMENT DEFECT THAT LIKELY PRODUCED THE WRONG READ: (status>>8)&0xff evaluates to 0 for a signal death, and p4exec prints child exit code = 0 for a SIGSEGV. LOCATED IN PRISTINE SOURCE: dcrt0.cc:646 cygheap_fixup_in_child(true) -> cygheap.cc:102 child_copy(child_proc_info->parent, false, "cygheap", ...); forks counterpart is dcrt0.cc:587 with the SAME handle field and it succeeds. TWO MECHANISMS ELIMINATED BY READING CONTROL FLOW RATHER THAN GREP: spawn.cc:597 SetHandleInformation(parent, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, 0) is inside if (!iscygwin()) at spawn.cc:594 so NOT taken for a Cygwin exec - I formed that hypothesis from the grep hit and refuted it by reading the block; and permissions are not it because sigproc.cc:938 duplicates with bInheritHandle=TRUE and PROCESS_VM_READ for BOTH paths, only PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE being fork-only. BOTH CreateProcessW calls pass TRUE for inherit handles (fork.cc:374, spawn.cc:660). SO THE TWO PATHS ARE CONFIGURED IDENTICALLY AT SOURCE LEVEL YET THE HANDLE IS VALID IN A FORKED CHILD AND INVALID IN AN EXECD CHILD. OBSERVATION NOT A FIX: get_parent_handle() at dcrt0.cc:632-637 re-opens the parent by pid and parent_winpid is set unconditionally at spawn.cc:602, but dcrt0.cc:644 if (!dynamically_loaded || get_parent_handle()) short-circuits so the recovery is unreachable on the normal exec path. NOT ESTABLISHED: why the handle is invalid; x86_64 not measured.

title: Replicating the Cygwin handle mint faithfully in pure Win32
description: MEASURED ON THIS ARM64 HOST, BOTH PERMISSION SETS, AND IT BOUNDS THE PROBLEM. Replicated the exact sigproc.cc:938 call shape - DuplicateHandle(GetCurrentProcess(), GetCurrentProcess(), GetCurrentProcess(), &parent, perms, TRUE, 0) - then CreateProcessW with bInheritHandles=TRUE, passing the handle VALUE and a pinned pattern buffer address as command-line data, and having the child perform the operation child_copy actually performs, ReadProcessMemory of the parent memory. ARM 1 exec set perms=0x101018 (PQLI|PROCESS_VM_READ|PROCESS_VM_OPERATION|SYNCHRONIZE): GetHandleInformation in the parent returns flags=0x1, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT ACTUALLY SET; child sees the handle VALID at the SAME VALUE with flags=0x1; ReadProcessMemory OK, 64 bytes, pattern A0-A7 intact. ARM 2 fork set perms=0x101058 (same plus PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE): IDENTICAL on every line. THREE RESULTS. (1) bInheritHandle=TRUE on a duplicated PSEUDO-handle IS HONOURED - the flag is observably set, not merely requested, closing the requested-versus-observed gap FOR PLAIN WIN32. (2) THE PERMISSION-SET ASYMMETRY IS DEFINITIVELY NOT THE CAUSE - I dismissed it earlier by READING and it is now dismissed by MEASUREMENT; PROCESS_DUP_HANDLE changes nothing about inheritance or the read. (3) ReadProcessMemory across an inherited process handle WORKS. BOUND STATED PRECISELY: NOTHING IN THE OS-LEVEL MECHANISM EXPLAINS THE FAILURE, so for a filing the platform does what is asked of it in a minimal reproduction and the anomaly lies in the runtime own path between mint and read. EXPLICIT NON-SUBSTITUTION: this does NOT close the requested-versus-observed gap INSIDE the Cygwin runtime - my probe mints and spawns in a plain process while the runtime does considerably more in between, and the reading process may not be the one I model. THE IN-SITU GetHandleInformation CHECK IS STILL REQUIRED.

title: Retracting my tlsoffsets good-content counter-argument
description: MY EIGHTH ERROR, RETRACTED IN FULL, CAUGHT BY DEMONSTRATION RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. That is the same shape as reasoning from evidence location to write location - my withdrawn geometric exclusion - so it is a REPEAT of an error class I had already catalogued, which is worse than a new one. WHAT SURVIVED AND WAS ADOPTED: my WIDTH objection was correct. The script emits const uint32_t (4-byte), c63ab774 .xword probe tested an 8-byte long, and for the 4-byte type aarch64 emits .word - which /\s*\.long\s+/ never matches. So the ORIGINAL .word claim was right and the correction of it was the error; my objection forced the measurement that settled it. title: Adopting mechanical precondition checks in harnesses
description: ADOPTED. Fifth self-caught harness failure was the most instructive: I had personally measured Git for Windows msys-2.0.dll as DllCharacteristics=0x0000 hours earlier and STILL reached for it as an ASLR test subject. title: RESOLVED - the b=0 anomaly was a free-list pointer; my disconfirmation was wrong
description: FULLY RESOLVED, AND MY EARLIER DISCONFIRMATION WAS WRONG. RESOLUTION VIA A TEST THAT ASSUMES NO SIZES: find the entry whose prev points at 0x8000068f0 - it is 0x80001e900, span 0x18010 = 98,320 bytes, minus the 16-byte header = 98,304 = bucket_val[23]. So the block is 98,304 bytes (bucket 23), NOT 32. Then the full bucket array: buckets[23] = 0x8000068f0. THE ENTRY IS ON A FREE LIST. It was allocated for the cygfork path, then FREED; _cfree stores ptr (next free block) in the union, and as the only entry in bucket 23 list ptr = NULL, WHICH READS BYTE-IDENTICALLY TO b=0. My "b=0" was never a bucket index. NEIGHBOURS ALL RECONCILE: 0x8000048a0 union=0xc span 0x810 = bucket_val[12]=2048; 0x8000050b0 union=0xf span 0x1810 = bucket_val[15]=6144; 0x8000068c0 union=0 span 0x30 = bucket_val[0]=32 GENUINELY bucket 0. MY ERROR: I printed buckets[0..15] when NBUCKETS IS 32 - I had read the 32-entry bucket_val table MYSELF and still wrote a loop bound of 16, then reported a confident negative. FOURTH ERROR OF THE DAY AND THE WORST-FORMED: AN INCOMPLETE SCAN REPORTED AS A NEGATIVE RESULT, the same failure class I have catalogued all day - a detector that could not fire on the true answer because it never looked there. CONSEQUENCES CORRECTED TO 68c032ba: (1) "free-list explanation tested and gone" deleted - it is tested and CONFIRMED; (2) my inference that this strengthened their b=6 finding is VOID, because on x86_64 the union holds a free-list pointer not a bucket index, so comparing it to an ARM64 b=6 compares different kinds of value; (3) the live possibility they should record instead is that ARM64 may simply have the block STILL ALLOCATED at sample time while x86_64 has it freed - an allocation-lifetime difference, not corruption - and a walker reading only the union cannot distinguish that from a real divergence. DISCRIMINATOR PASSED ON: the span test (find the entry whose prev is 0x8000068F0; the gap gives true size) is the only size measurement not dependent on a union whose meaning changes with allocation state. UNAFFECTED: 0x8000068F8 should hold 0x8000068C0 (prev is at +8 and survives free), and the block holds the cygfork path (now known to be stale freed content, which still identifies its use).

title: Verifying the quoted() overlapping-strcpy diagnosis from sealed source
description: MEASURED, VERIFIED, EVERY ELEMENT CONFIRMED - AND THE DIAGNOSIS WAS NOT MINE. c63ab774 reported applying memmove at dcrt0.cc:165,167 in quoted(), crediting me with the diagnosis. I DID NOT SUPPLY IT (see misattribution row). I verified it anyway from the sealed pristine source because it is cheap and it is my role. TREE-WIDE SWEEP of all .cc/.c/.h under winsup/cygwin for strcpy with src derived from dst: EXACTLY TWO SITES, both in dcrt0.cc - line 165 strcpy (cmd, cmd + 1) and line 167 strcpy (p, p + 1). Function confirmed as quoted() declared at dcrt0.cc:156-157. Both are dst = src - 1, i.e. a left-shift by one over an overlapping buffer = textbook UB. The count, the file, both line numbers, the function name and the dst=src-1 shape ALL CHECK. memmove is the correct fix. INCIDENTAL OBSERVATION, not a defect: line 164 declares an inner char *p that SHADOWS the outer char *p at line 159; the return at 168 returns the inner one and is correct. Also confirmed correct by design: quote is captured at line 160 BEFORE the line 165 shift, so it still holds the original opening quote when used by strchrnul at 166. CLASSIFICATION THAT MATTERS AND NOBODY HAS STATED: THIS IS UPSTREAM CYGWIN CODE, NOT PORT-SPECIFIC. Overlapping strcpy is UB on every target; it survives on x86_64 by implementation accident. So this is an UPSTREAM-FILING CANDIDATE that is architecture-RELEVANT but not ARM64-only, same class as the child_copy stale-error and unchecked VirtualAlloc latent defects. DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, AND LABELLED AS SUCH: the reported signature - two chars dropped, two duplicated, TOTAL LENGTH UNCHANGED at 24 - is the fingerprint of a CHUNKED/VECTORISED copy re-reading source bytes it has already overwritten, which is what an optimised AArch64 strcpy would do and a byte-at-a-time forward copy would not. I have NOT disassembled the aarch64 strcpy and do not assert this. METHOD POINT WORTH PROPAGATING: because length is preserved, a strlen check, a null-termination check AND a round-trip length comparison ALL PASS on corrupted data. Only byte-for-byte comparison catches it; their length sweep 1..40 is the right instrument.

title: Verifying the named corrupting store instruction
description: MEASURED, VERIFIED, MATCH. c63ab774 named the corrupting store as str x4,[sp,#24] at RVA 0x6CD8 in _dll_crt0 of new-msys-2.0.dll. I DECODED BOTH RAW ENCODINGS INDEPENDENTLY rather than accept the reading. 0xaa1203e4: sf=1 opc=01 fixed(28:24)=01010 shift=0 N=0 Rm=18 Rn=31(xzr) imm6=0 Rd=4 => ORR shifted-register 64-bit => mov x4, x18. MATCH. 0xf9000fe4: size=3 fixed(29:24)=111001 opc=00 imm12=3 (x8 = +24) Rn=31(sp) Rt=4 => STR immediate unsigned-offset 64-bit => str x4,[sp,#24]. MATCH. ARITHMETIC VERIFIED AGAINST MY OWN MEASURED StackBase: StackBase=0x800000000, sp=StackBase-16=0x7fffffff0, [sp,#24]=0x800000008, cygheap+8=0x800000008, IDENTICAL; reach 32 bytes against 16 available. Both operands - value and address - reproduce independent measurements, so the pair is over-determined. MY LOAD-BEARING CONTRIBUTION: the measurement that main-thread StackBase is exactly 0x800000000, byte-identical to the cygheap base because THREAD_STORAGE_HIGH and CYGHEAP_STORAGE_LOW are the same address; their sp arithmetic runs through it. AND THE CONCRETE COST OF MY WORST ERROR IS NOW VISIBLE: my withdrawn GEOMETRIC EXCLUSION had argued that a write to cygheap->chain would have clobbered the head rather than the 44th entry prev, ruling out head-writing mechanisms. THE TRUE ANSWER IS A HEAD-WRITE. Had that exclusion stood it would have excluded the correct answer; withdrawing it re-opened the door. NEW ERROR CLASS RECORDED from their causal story, distinct from the seven catalogued: A CORRECT ARCHITECTURAL FACT APPLIED TO THE DOCUMENTED PURPOSE OF AN INSTRUCTION THAT HAD TWO PURPOSES - x86 subq $32 also supplied headroom, and x86_64 tolerates its removal because locals sit at negative offsets from rbp while AArch64 spills at positive offsets from sp. STRUCTURAL LESSON: every scan asked what stores the TEB DELIBERATELY, and nothing does - it is an ordinary spill whose value happened to be the TEB because the TEB was live across VirtualFree. The question was unanswerable as posed. HONEST LIMIT PRESERVED AND ENDORSED: naming is not fixing; no rebuild has demonstrated fork passes.

title: Verifying the hookapi ARM64 classification root cause from source
description: VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY SOURCE, CHAIN CONFIRMED END TO END. hookapi.cc:43-50 PEHeaderFromHModule contains an explicit machine allowlist: switch (pNTHeader->FileHeader.Machine) { case IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64: break; default: return NULL; } with the comment "Return valid PIMAGE_NT_HEADERS only for supported architectures." An 0xAA64 PE falls to default and returns NULL. CHAIN: spawn.cc:1225 real_path.set_cygexec (hook_or_detect_cygwin (buf, NULL, ...)) -> hookapi.cc:333 hook_or_detect_cygwin -> hookapi.cc:336 pExeNTHdr = PEHeaderFromHModule (hm) returns NULL -> set_cygexec(NULL) via path.h:260 -> iscygwin() false -> spawn.cc:594 if (!iscygwin()) TRUE -> spawn.cc:597 SetHandleInformation (parent, HANDLE_FLAG_INHERIT, 0) STRIPS THE BIT. title: Establishing that the version gap does not confound the cygheap differential
description: MEASURED, partially retires a standing caveat. The cygheap differential rests on upstream Git for Windows msys-2.0.dll 3.6.9 - a DIFFERENT VERSION WE DID NOT BUILD - which c63ab774 flagged and I repeated as the remaining limitation, and which motivated commissioning an x86_64 build of our own sources. RE-WALKING upstream 3.6.9 x86_64 with the corrected bucket_val sizing gives 0x8000048a0 b=12 size 2048; 0x8000050b0 b=15 size 6144; 0x8000068c0 b=0 size 32 owning the username; 0x8000068f0 b=0 size 32. OUR ARM64 BUILD PRODUCES THE SAME ADDRESSES AND THE SAME BUCKET INDICES - b=15 at 0x8000050B0, username entry at 0x8000068C0, next at 0x8000068F0, contiguous to the byte. SO THE ALLOCATION SEQUENCE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS A VERSION GAP AND AN ARCHITECTURE GAP. If the version difference were confounding this measurement it would surface exactly there, and it does not. STATED NO MORE STRONGLY THAN: version is not a plausible confounder FOR THE SPECIFIC STRUCTURE UNDER EXAMINATION; it does not retire the caveat in general and other differences between 3.6.9 and our tree could matter elsewhere. PRACTICAL EFFECT: moves the x86_64 build from PREREQUISITE FOR DEFINITIVENESS to NICE-TO-HAVE CORROBORATION, which matters because that build currently has no host to run on.

title: RESOLVED: the 414-of-424 missing base relocations are NOT a defect — ASLR was wrongly enabled; upstream Cygwin never relocates the DLL
description: RECORDED 2026-09-03 from the link owner root-cause, and it ANSWERS THE OPEN QUESTION I had posed. I had reframed the problem as "why does the linker emit base relocations for 10 of 424 identical ADDR64 relocations and drop 414", suspecting a section-, order- or threshold-dependent linker defect. THE TRUE ANSWER IS THAT THE MISSING BASE RELOCATIONS ARE NOT A DEFECT AT ALL. The Cygwin autoload thunks embed absolute 64-bit addresses by design, and upstream this is HARMLESS BECAUSE THE CYGWIN RUNTIME DLL IS NEVER RELOCATED: fork() copies the address space and requires the DLL at the SAME address in parent and child, so the image must load at its preferred base. THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THAT THE LINK ENABLED ASLR. DllCharacteristics measured as 0x0160 = HIGH_ENTROPY_VA | DYNAMIC_BASE | NX_COMPAT. Makefile.am passes no --disable-dynamicbase and MODERN BINUTILS DEFAULTS IT ON, so the port inherited an ASLR that upstream never had. With ASLR on, the loader moves the image and every absolute address lacking a base relocation becomes stale, so the first autoload call branches into unmapped memory. Relinking with -Wl,--disable-dynamicbase -Wl,--disable-high-entropy-va yields DllCharacteristics 0x0100 and THE 0xC0000005 IS GONE, replaced by a clean LoadLibrary refusal with GetLastError 193 ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT — a diagnosable failure rather than a hard fault. THIS VINDICATES MY DIFFERENTIAL RESULT AND EXPLAINS IT: I proved by building the construct for both architectures that x86_64 and aarch64 emit STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL absolute quads and IDENTICAL ADDR64 relocations, and concluded the defect could not lie in the source construct or the assembler. That conclusion was correct. The reason x86_64 Cygwin works is NOT that its linker behaves differently — it is that upstream x86_64 Cygwin DOES NOT ENABLE ASLR, so the identical missing base relocations never matter. My inference that the fault must lie downstream of assembly was right; the specific guess that it was a base-relocation-emission defect was wrong, and the real cause is an image-characteristics defect. NOTE THE COROBORATING DATUM: the image was observed loading at 0x7ffdac3c0000 rather than its preferred 0x180000000, which directly proves the loader was relocating it and is the precondition the ASLR diagnosis requires.

title: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT: ARM64 .pdata entries are 8 bytes — 5,975 entries, not 3,983
description: MEASURED DIRECTLY FROM THE DLL 2026-09-03, settling the arithmetic rather than arguing it. I parsed the section table of msys-2.0.dll from its own PE headers: .pdata VirtualSize = 47,800 bytes. AT 8 BYTES PER ENTRY, THE ARM64 PE RUNTIME_FUNCTION SIZE, THAT IS 47,800 / 8 = 5,975 EXACTLY, REMAINDER ZERO. At the x64 12-byte layout it would be 3,983 with REMAINDER 4. THE COORDINATOR CORRECTION IS THEREFORE RIGHT AND THE 3,983 FIGURE IS WRONG. ARM64 PE RUNTIME_FUNCTION is a 4-byte function-start RVA plus 4 bytes of unwind data, either packed or an .xdata RVA; the 12-byte Begin/End/UnwindInfo triple is the x64 layout. CORROBORATION FROM MY OWN EARLIER WORK: when I analysed sigfe.o I used 8 bytes and got 7,912 / 8 = 989 entries EXACTLY MATCHING 989 .seh_proc directives, which independently confirms the 8-byte size on this architecture. THE GENERAL LESSON, AND IT IS THE SAME FAMILY AS .align MEANING 2^N ON AArch64 VERSUS N BYTES ON x86: a construct that exists on both architectures under the same name with different semantics, where carrying the x86 assumption across silently yields a plausible-looking wrong answer rather than an error. THE TELL WAS PRESENT AND WAS MISSED: AN EXACT DIVISION THAT DOES NOT DIVIDE EXACTLY IS A DEFECT IN THE MODEL, NOT A ROUNDING DETAIL. Any count derived by dividing a size by a per-entry width must report the remainder, and a non-zero remainder must invalidate the model rather than be discarded. ALSO MEASURED WHILE THERE: Machine 0xaa64, 23 sections, .text VirtualSize 1,929,044, .xdata 67,352, .edata 36,470, .idata 15,648, and TimeDateStamp 0x6a998f9d = 2026-09-03 15:17:49 UTC located at file offset 0x88.

title: CRITICAL CORRECTION: the reported crash is a .NET managed exception in the TEST HARNESS, not a fault in msys-2.0.dll — and LoadLibrary SUCCEEDED
description: MEASURED AND ANALYSED 2026-09-03, and this materially changes the reading of the execution attempt. THE CRASH IS NOT IN THE DLL. From files\runtest\crash.txt, MEASURED VALUES: EXCEPTION_CODE 0xE0434352; EXCEPTION_FLAGS 0x00000081; EXCEPTION_ADDRESS 0x00007FFE5E79BF54; MODULE_BASE 0x00007FFDAFAA0000; RVA_FROM_BASE 0xAECFBF54 which is 2,932,850,516; NumberParameters 5; AV_OPERATION -2146233087; AV_TARGET_ADDRESS 0x0000000000000000. DERIVED FROM DOCUMENTED CONSTANTS: 0xE0434352 IS THE CLR MANAGED-EXCEPTION SEH CODE used by .NET, not a native access violation, whose code would be 0xC0000005; and AV_OPERATION -2146233087 is 0x80131501, which is COR_E_SYSTEM, the HRESULT for System.Exception. NumberParameters of 5 is also the CLR managed-exception shape rather than the 2 parameters of an access violation. DERIVED BY ARITHMETIC, AND DECISIVE: the exception address 0x7FFE5E79BF54 minus the module base 0x7FFDAFAA0000 gives roughly 2.93 GB, whereas the DLL IS ONLY 30.8 MB, SO THE FAULTING ADDRESS LIES FAR OUTSIDE THE MODULE. The reported RVA_FROM_BASE is therefore meaningless — it is the arithmetic difference between two unrelated addresses, and the harness mislabelled generic CLR ExceptionInformation fields as access-violation operation and target fields. CONCLUSION: the exception was raised by the PowerShell/.NET test harness (r03-veh.ps1), NOT by code inside msys-2.0.dll. AND THE POSITIVE RESULT THAT THIS MISREADING MASKS, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THE FILE: crash.txt itself records "map-only base : 0x7FFDAFAA0000" and "full load returned 0x7FFDAFAA0000 lasterror=0". THAT MEANS LoadLibrary SUCCEEDED — the loader accepted the image, resolved its imports, ran to a valid base address, and set no error. A native ARM64 msys-2.0.dll LOADED. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE: it proves the image is well-formed enough for the Windows loader to map and bind it, which is a genuine and significant first. It does NOT prove any runtime function works, does NOT prove initialisation completed correctly, and does NOT prove anything about signals, fork or printf, none of which had run at the point this file was written. The subsequent harness exception says nothing either way about the DLL.

title: DISPROVEN by differential: the autoload absolute-quad construct is NOT ARM64-only — x86_64 emits the identical relocations, so the defect is at LINK time
description: MEASURED 2026-09-03 by building the same construct for both architectures and comparing, the same x86-versus-ARM64 differential method that settled the SEH question. THE HYPOTHESIS TESTED: that x86_64 uses PC-relative addressing rather than absolute quads, which would make the missing-base-relocation defect structurally ARM64-only. IT IS DISPROVEN. FIRST, AT SOURCE LEVEL, MEASURED FROM autoload.cc: the x86_64 thunk at lines 126-150 and the aarch64 thunk at lines 164-195 BOTH emit the SAME TWO ABSOLUTE QUADS — "2:.quad ."#dllname"_info" and "3:.quad 1b". The x86_64 body reaches them with RIP-relative loads (movq 3f(%rip),%rax) and the aarch64 body with a PC-relative literal load (ldr x16, 3f) and adr, but THE PAYLOAD SLOTS THEMSELVES ARE ABSOLUTE 64-BIT VALUES ON BOTH. The addressing used to REACH the slot is PC-relative on both; the CONTENT of the slot is an absolute address on both. SECOND, AT OBJECT LEVEL, MEASURED by assembling a minimal reproduction of the construct for each target with the same clang and dumping relocations with llvm-objdump: for x86_64-w64-mingw32 the object carries IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR64 at offsets 0x0a and 0x12 against .foo_info and .foo_autoload_text; for aarch64-w64-mingw32 it carries IMAGE_REL_ARM64_ADDR64 at offsets 0x0c and 0x14 against the same two targets. STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL — two absolute 64-bit relocations per thunk on both architectures, differing only in the offsets, which follow from the differing instruction sizes, and in the architecture-specific relocation type name. I ALSO CONFIRMED THE SAME RESULT WITH THE PROGRAMME OWN aarch64-pc-cygwin-as AND objdump, which independently produced the identical two IMAGE_REL_ARM64_ADDR64 records, so this is not an artifact of using clang. CONCLUSION, AND IT RELOCATES THE DEFECT SHARPLY. The assembler is CORRECT: it emits proper ADDR64 relocations for every absolute quad on both architectures. Therefore the reported condition that 414 of 424 absolute quads carry NO BASE RELOCATION IN THE FINAL IMAGE CANNOT ORIGINATE IN THE SOURCE CONSTRUCT OR IN ASSEMBLY. It must arise at LINK TIME, in the step that converts object-level ADDR64 relocations into entries in the image .reloc base-relocation directory. NOT TESTED BY ME, AND STATED AS SUCH: I did not run the link step or inspect the resulting .reloc directory, so I have localised the defect by elimination rather than observed it directly. A REASONABLE BUT UNTESTED INFERENCE worth flagging rather than asserting: x86_64 Cygwin has shipped this identical construct for years, so the linker evidently handles it correctly for AMD64, which would place the defect specifically in the ARM64 path of base-relocation emission or in how the custom "wx" autoload sections are gathered for ARM64. THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW BETTER POSED: not "why does the ARM64 thunk use absolute quads" — both do — but "why does the linker emit base relocations for 10 of 424 identical ADDR64 relocations and drop the other 414", which suggests something section-, order- or threshold-dependent rather than a wholesale failure.

title: VERIFIED TO FULL PROTOCOL: native ARM64 Git runs on this host — all five points, including live-process emulation status
description: VERIFIED 2026-09-03 to the five-point protocol. BINARY: C:\Users\crutkasLocal\AppData\Local\Temp\arm64git\root\clangarm64\bin\git.exe, 4,056,064 bytes, sha256 dc8c9ef26d1d164779bd833eca6766afcec8f2fbd71ea6cc40b5e794be395449. POINT 1, RAW COFF READ, MEASURED BY ME: I read offset 0x3C to find the PE header offset, verified the PE signature bytes, and read the Machine field directly — 0xaa64, ARM64. Not taken from any tool summary string. POINT 2, LIVE-PROCESS EMULATION STATUS, WHICH WAS THE UNREPORTED POINT AND IS NOW MEASURED: I launched the binary as a live process using "git hash-object --stdin" so it would block on stdin, and called IsWow64Process2 against the real process handle. RESULT: ProcessMachine = 0x0000, which by the API contract means the process is NOT running under WOW64, i.e. NATIVE; NativeMachine = 0xaa64. THE COORDINATOR REASONING IS CONFIRMED MECHANICALLY RATHER THAN ACCEPTED: Windows on Arm emulates x86 and x64 but does not emulate ARM64, so an 0xAA64 image on an ARM64 host is native by construction, and the emulation check exists to catch the CONVERSE case of an x64 binary masquerading as success. The live process confirms it directly. POINT 3, MODULES ACTUALLY BOUND BY THE LIVE PROCESS rather than files sitting in a directory, which are different claims: I enumerated the running process module list and read each module Machine field from its own COFF header. 23 MODULES BOUND, ZERO NON-ARM64. These include git.exe itself, ntdll, KERNEL32, KERNELBASE, ucrtbase, ADVAPI32, msvcrt, sechost, RPCRT4, WS2_32, USER32, win32u, GDI32, gdi32full, msvcp_win, CRYPTBASE, bcryptPrimitives, IMM32 and ntmarta from C:\Windows\System32, plus libintl-8.dll, zlib1.dll, libpcre2-8-0.dll and libiconv-2.dll from the package tree. Every one 0xaa64. POINT 4, WHAT THE RUN DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE, stated below. POINT 5, THE REFERENCE-VERSUS-OUR-CHAIN DISTINCTION, held. THE THREE CLAIMS, KEPT SEPARATE AND NOT MERGED: (a) NATIVE ARM64 GIT RUNS ON THIS HARDWARE — VERIFIED, natively, with a fully ARM64 bound module set. (b) OUR TOOLCHAIN BUILDS IT — NOT SHOWN BY THIS RUN AT ALL; this is a PREBUILT MSYS2 clangarm64 package and session 2918d1f1 owns that separate claim. (c) THE MSYS2 RUNTIME WORKS — UNTOUCHED, AND NOW MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: I searched the entire package root and msys-2.0.dll IS ABSENT FROM IT, so nothing in this tree could load the runtime even in principle. The honest headline is that the TARGET IS PROVEN ACHIEVABLE and we now hold a REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION to diff our own build against.

title: VERIFIED AND STRENGTHENED: the 14-script shell-dependent list is correct, and the C-builtin claims hold under a provably sh-free PATH with effect evidence
description: VERIFIED 2026-09-03, and this verification is STRONGER THAN THE ORIGINAL because of the sh-reachability finding below. INDEPENDENT CLASSIFICATION: I read the first two bytes of every git-* file in clangarm64/libexec/git-core and classified MZ as PE and anything else as script. RESULT: 25 files, 11 PE, 14 SCRIPTS — an EXACT match to the reported list. The 14 are git-difftool--helper, git-filter-branch, git-instaweb, git-merge-octopus, git-merge-one-file, git-merge-resolve, git-mergetool, git-mergetool--lib, git-quiltimport, git-request-pull, git-sh-i18n, git-sh-setup, git-submodule and git-web--browse. THE LOAD-BEARING CONDITION, AND THE ORIGINAL EVIDENCE MAY NOT HAVE MET IT: the claim depends on NO sh being reachable. I established by exact enumeration that THE AMBIENT PATH ON THIS HOST DOES CONTAIN SHELLS — C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe, C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe and C:\Users\crutkasLocal\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\bash.exe, from an existing x86-64 Git for Windows installation. SO ANY TEST RUN WITH THE INHERITED PATH WOULD HAVE HAD sh AVAILABLE AND WOULD PROVE NOTHING. I therefore re-ran every command under a CONTROLLED PATH of exactly the package bin directory plus C:\Windows\System32, and verified by direct probing that sh.exe, bash.exe and dash.exe are ALL UNREACHABLE on it. EFFECT-BASED EVIDENCE, NOT EXIT CODES, because a command that exits 0 having done nothing is indistinguishable from success by status alone: git stash returned 0 AND created refs/stash AND reverted the working tree from "two" back to "one" AND populated git stash list. git bisect start returned 0 AND created both .git/BISECT_START and .git/BISECT_LOG. git add -p, fed "y", returned 0 AND actually moved the staged set from empty to a.txt. git rebase master returned 0 AND genuinely rewrote history — the parent of HEAD moved from 347e4d90 to 8380d368, which is exactly the master commit, with the log showing topic1 replayed on top of master1. THE DECISIVE NEGATIVE CONTROL, which is what makes the whole test meaningful: git submodule status in the SAME sh-free environment FAILED with exit 128 and "fatal: submodule appears to be a git command, but we were not able to execute it". So the environment genuinely breaks sh-dependent commands, and the four that passed did not pass by accident. CONCLUSION: THE CLAIM IS TRUE AND THE OUTDATED LIST SHOULD BE CORRECTED. rebase, bisect, add -p and stash are C builtins in Git 2.55 and are NOT runtime-gated. That materially shrinks what msys-2.0.dll is needed FOR and raises the value of the MINGW track. NOTE THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN THE RUNTIME CASE ENTIRELY: 14 genuine scripts remain, chiefly filter-branch, mergetool/difftool, submodule, request-pull, quiltimport, instaweb, web--browse and the octopus/resolve merge strategies, plus the git-sh-setup and git-sh-i18n helpers and any shell-script repo hooks.

description: VERIFIED 2026-09-03 for session c63ab774. ALL LINK CLAIMS HOLD. title: ANSWERED: the two .idata alignment fixes are REDUNDANT for these libraries — but only because of a measured property, and the import-lib fix is strictly more robust
description: MEASURED MECHANICALLY 2026-09-03, answering the coordinator question of whether the linker-script fix and the import-library fix are redundant, complementary, or one insufficient. THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: I enumerated every .idata$4 and .idata$5 input section across all four import libraries and checked each size modulo 8. RESULT: libkernel32 1,642 sections, libntdll 2,240, libadvapi32 881, libuser32 963 — 5,726 members in total — and ZERO sections in ANY library are not a multiple of 8. The size distribution is degenerate: in libkernel32, 1,641 of the .idata$5 sections are EXACTLY 8 bytes and one is 0 bytes, and .idata$4 is identical. THE LOGIC THAT FOLLOWS: if the linker script forces the group start to 8-byte alignment, then because every contributor is exactly 8 bytes, the running offset is a multiple of 8 at every contributor boundary, so every IAT entry lands 8-aligned automatically. At such an offset a declared 2**2 requirement is ALREADY SATISFIED, so the linker inserts no padding and nothing shifts. THE INPUT-SECTION ALIGNMENT ATTRIBUTE IS THEREFORE IRRELEVANT TO THE FINAL LAYOUT FOR THESE LIBRARIES. ANSWER: THE TWO FIXES ARE REDUNDANT — EITHER ALONE SUFFICES, GIVEN AN 8-ALIGNED GROUP START. CRITICAL QUALIFICATION, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS FOR AN UPSTREAM PATCH: the linker-script fix is sufficient ONLY BECAUSE OF A MEASURED PROPERTY OF THESE PARTICULAR LIBRARIES, not as a matter of principle. If any contributor were NOT a multiple of 8, the running offset would become misaligned and a declared 2**2 alignment would NOT correct it, so subsequent entries would drift and the truncations would return. THE IMPORT-LIBRARY FIX IS STRICTLY MORE ROBUST because raising the declared alignment to 2**3 forces the linker to 8-align each section regardless of what preceded it, making correctness independent of both the linker script and the contributor-size property. SO: redundant today, but not equally safe. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CORRECT UPSTREAM PATCH: the ROOT CAUSE is in dlltool, which emits 2**2 alignment for sections holding 8-byte IAT and ILT entries on a 64-bit target. That is why the same defect would affect ANY project linking ARM64 PE against dlltool-generated import libraries, not just msys2-runtime. A linker-script change is a LOCAL WORKAROUND IN ONE PROJECT; the dlltool alignment is the GENERAL FIX. Investigation-only and an IOU candidate; no contact and no patch submission. I CORRECT MY OWN EARLIER CAVEAT: I had recorded that .idata$4 remaining at 2**2 was structurally wrong and a live runtime risk. THAT IS SOFTENED BY MEASUREMENT: because every .idata$4 contributor is also exactly 8 bytes, the Import Lookup Table entries also land 8-aligned in the final image whenever the group start is aligned, regardless of the declared attribute. What is wrong is therefore the DECLARED ATTRIBUTE, not the resulting LAYOUT. The residual risk is much smaller than I first stated and I should not have implied a probable runtime fault.

title: ANSWERED: .seh_handler = 0 is BY DESIGN — x86_64 emits zero handlers too, and the AArch64 unwind data is well-formed
description: TASK 1 ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-03. THE QUESTION CLOSES: ZERO .seh_handler IS CORRECT AND IS NOT A GAP. DECISIVE COMPARISON: I ran the STOCK gendef (gendef.orig, md5 ba09b7e4, the unfixed upstream script) with --cpu=x86_64 against the same cygwin.din, and the x86_64 reference output emits EXACTLY THE SAME SEH DIRECTIVE PROFILE as the new AArch64 backend: 989 .seh_proc, 989 .seh_endprologue, 989 .seh_endproc, 1001 .seh_pushreg, 1 .seh_setframe, 1 .seh_stackalloc, AND .seh_handler = 0. IDENTICAL ON BOTH ARCHITECTURES. So the AArch64 backend reproduces the x86_64 behaviour exactly; the earlier report of "balanced 989/989/989" was simply a misstatement of the third figure, and zero handlers is the correct design rather than an omission. THE SECOND AND MORE IMPORTANT HALF — CAN THE TRAMPOLINES BE UNWOUND THROUGH? A region that is unwound THROUGH needs correct unwind data even with no handler of its own, which is a different requirement from having a handler. MEASURED, all from my independently assembled sigfe.o (sha256 cfcba2a91b0291e5bad8298570d5f3f6348434a2161b8a1ca9bcf79b1d64d21c): the object contains BOTH .pdata (0x1ee8 = 7,912 bytes) and .xdata (0x1efc = 7,932 bytes). ARM64 .pdata entries are 8 bytes, so 7,912 / 8 = 989 ENTRIES, WHICH EXACTLY MATCHES THE 989 .seh_proc REGIONS — one unwind entry per trampoline, none missing. Relocations in .pdata number 1,978, i.e. EXACTLY TWO PER ENTRY, and they are of type IMAGE_REL_ARM64_ADDR32NB against .text and .xdata respectively — the correct RVA-based relocation type for PE unwind tables. DERIVED, from the documented ARM64 .xdata header layout: the first record word 0x0800000c decodes as Function Length 12 words = 48 bytes, Vers 0, X = 0, E = 0, EpilogCount 0, CodeWords 1. THE X BIT IS ZERO, MEANING NO EXCEPTION DATA, WHICH IS INTERNALLY CONSISTENT WITH THE ABSENCE OF .seh_handler — the unwind record correctly DECLARES no handler rather than claiming one and omitting it. The unwind code stream begins 0xE4, the end opcode, with 0xE3 nop padding, so the code sequence is properly terminated. CONCLUSION: the unwind information is COMPLETE, WELL-FORMED AND SELF-CONSISTENT, not merely assemblable, and the trampolines can be unwound through. This is a clean negative result — a real question asked and answered with no defect found. DISCLOSED PROCESS ERROR OF MY OWN: stock gendef writes to a FIXED filename sigfe.s in the current directory, so running it in my scratch OVERWROTE my copy of the AArch64 sigfe.s. Contained entirely to my own /root/xc-verify scratch, no other directory touched, and the authoritative source in session-state was untouched; I restored it and re-verified sha256 8df387e99728900d..., and confirmed the previously assembled sigfe.o was unaffected with its hash still matching.

title: RETRACTED: the DISPATCHER_CONTEXT "cross-validation" was COMMON-CAUSE, not independent
description:
RETRACTED AND CORRECTED 2026-09-03 BY THE COORDINATOR SESSION AFTER SOURCE VERIFICATION. I previously recorded this as "two independent methods, identical answer" confirming the sealed ABI session mangling analysis. THAT INFERENCE WAS WRONG, and I am retracting it. WHAT I GOT WRONG: the linker error showing _ZN9exception7myfaultEP17_EXCEPTION_RECORDPvP8_CONTEXTP25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 is NOT an independent derivation. IT IS AN ECHO OF A STRING THE SOURCE HARD-CODES. I verified the sealed backup patch (arm64-port.patch, 49823 bytes, sha256 e2068db8de17df27cedc3e1fe61c1f182fac1347df22da351e2ada75e130089f) and it literally emits that token at patch line 1035 as "P25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, @except", with the assumption stated in a comment at line 953: "winnt.h names the struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64". So BOTH observations trace to THE SAME SOURCE TOKEN. Two observations sharing a common cause are NOT mutual confirmation, and I should have asked what would have to be true for the second observation to be independent before recording it as such. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is more interesting than either verdict: THE CORRECT MANGLED NAME IS W32API-VERSION-DEPENDENT. Verified directly at source. In mingw-w64 MASTER winnt.h (10781 lines): line 2465 typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, line 2478 closes it as DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 and PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, and line 2481 does "typedef DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, *PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT". Since C++ mangling uses the UNDERLYING STRUCT TAG rather than the typedef name, PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT on ARM64 under MASTER genuinely mangles to P25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64. In w32api v12.0.0 winnt.h (10390 lines), which is the version the build PINS, there are THREE separate plain "struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT" definitions at lines 2074-2078, 2310-2314 and 2974-2978 — one per architecture block — and the identifier _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 DOES NOT APPEAR ANYWHERE IN THE FILE. Under v12.0.0 the correct mangling is therefore P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. CONSEQUENCE: the ABI session MEASUREMENT WAS CORRECT FOR THE HEADERS IT USED, and its method of compiling a probe and reading it with llvm-nm rather than guessing REMAINS RIGHT AND IS NOT IMPUGNED. What is wrong is the hard-coded assumption that the ARM64 name is fixed, and my inference that the linker error confirmed it.

COORDINATOR ADDENDUM 2026-09-03, completing the retraction. The coordinator has WITHDRAWN the instruction under which this was originally recorded, stating plainly that they ordered it and were wrong. THE CORRECT ACCOUNT, verified from both header sets: the CLANGARM64 toolchain winnt.h (405,341 bytes) DOES contain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, 2 occurrences, alongside 8 plain "struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT"; released w32api v12.0.0 contains NONE and declares plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT in all three architecture branches (verified by me at lines 2074, 2310 and 2974 of a 10,390-line file). SO BOTH MEASUREMENTS WERE CORRECT FOR THEIR OWN HEADER SET, and neither party made a measurement error — the error was entirely in the INFERENCE that the second observation corroborated the first. GENERALISED LESSON, to be recorded in place of the withdrawn claim: A DOWNSTREAM TOOL REPEATING A STRING THAT AN UPSTREAM ARTIFACT HARD-CODED IS NOT INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION. BEFORE TREATING TWO OBSERVATIONS AS MUTUAL CONFIRMATION, ESTABLISH WHETHER THE SECOND SOURCE DERIVED THE VALUE OR MERELY REPEATED IT. This belongs to the same measurement-error family as the git status staleness behind the NUL.exe misreport, the process filter that matched the substring "git" and counted fsmonitor daemons as compilers, and the unvalidated patch artifact that PowerShell had silently collapsed to a single line. The common thread across all four is TRUSTING A SIGNAL WITHOUT ESTABLISHING ITS PROVENANCE.

CLANGARM64 HEADER VERIFIED AT THE EXACT PATH, 2026-09-03, closing the open corroboration. File: C:\Users\crutkasLocal\.copilot\session-state\aabca41f-e845-47dd-97cd-bc99428bc7d4\files\arm64-local-workload\toolchain-root\clangarm64\include\winnt.h, 405,341 bytes, 10,796 lines, sha256 51f9430b73aa131e9c966d5b701557adc090e6f51f93caf51bdc4a8f91f46f2c. Earlier I could not find it because I searched only for SYSTEM installs (C:\msys64, C:\msys2, C:\tools) and it lives in SESSION STATE; my flag that I had corroborated the structural claim from a DIFFERENT artifact rather than the cited one was the right caution and is now closed properly. I WENT BEYOND OCCURRENCE COUNTING TO THE MECHANISM, which is stronger: line 2480 defines "typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 {" closing at 2493 as DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 and PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, and then lines 2495-2497 read "#if defined(_ARM64_) / typedef DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, *PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT / #endif". THAT ALIAS IS WHY THE MANGLING COMES OUT P25 ON THIS HEADER SET: C++ mangling uses the underlying struct tag, so PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT resolves to struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 *. PRECISION CORRECTION TO THE CITED COUNT, offered because it is the same error class this thread has been logging: the figure "2 occurrences of _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64" IS A SUBSTRING COUNT, NOT A SEMANTIC ONE. The two hits are line 2480 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 and line 3126 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64EC — and the latter is A DIFFERENT STRUCT for ARM64EC that merely CONTAINS the substring. There is exactly ONE genuine _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64. This is the identical failure mode to the process filter that matched the substring "git" and counted fsmonitor daemons as compilers. THE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED — the struct exists and drives the mangling via the 2496 alias — but the count should be recorded as 1 genuine plus 1 substring artifact. The 8 plain "struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT" occurrences are confirmed at 2102, 2103, 2104, 2106, 3106, 3107, 3108 and 3110.

THE NAME IS HEADER-SET-DEPENDENT AS VERIFIED FACT, not a two-way version quirk. Distinct header sets now measured, giving different answers: (1) CLANGARM64 405,341 B — genuine _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 aliased under #if defined(_ARM64_) => P25; (2) released w32api v12.0.0, 10,390 lines — ZERO _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 anywhere, three plain struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT blocks at 2074, 2310 and 2974 => P19; (3) mingw-w64 MASTER, 10,781 lines — _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 at 2465 with the alias at 2481 => P25; (4) coordinator-measured inside the SAME checkout, inst/.../w32api/winnt.h 387,345 B with ZERO ARM64 and 12 plain, versus mingw-w64/mingw-w64-tools/widl/include/winnt.h 264,325 B with FOUR ARM64 and 2 plain. THAT LAST PAIR IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE because the two headers DISAGREE INSIDE ONE CHECKOUT, settling the structural point from a source neither party originally cited, and it is INDEPENDENT rather than a repetition.

title: DISCREPANCY CORRECTED: the two longdouble.c preservation copies are NOT byte-identical — CRLF versus LF
description: MEASURED CORRECTION 2026-09-03. IT WAS REPORTED THAT longdouble.c IS "3,368 BYTES IN BOTH LOCATIONS". THAT IS NOT WHAT THE FILES SHOW. The two preservation copies DIFFER IN SIZE AND IN HASH: the c63ab774 evidence copy is 3,368 bytes with 152 BARE LF and 0 CRLF, sha256 aaf9785b057e5527e717c294a76f40a755ac0cd15735856cc7b2d4af827ff80b; the 724ee2e9 sealed-backup copy is 3,520 bytes with 152 CRLF and 0 bare LF, sha256 52d89409e33f27e195065d1cf0911e4d2c3052a8f8f0f6f2df9bce9181cb5c26. The delta is EXACTLY 152 BYTES, one per line, which is the signature of the line-ending difference. CONTENT IS SAFE AND THIS IS NOT A LOSS: after LF normalisation the two are IDENTICAL, both hashing to aaf9785b057e5527e717c294a76f40a755ac0cd15735856cc7b2d4af827ff80b, confirmed by direct case-sensitive string comparison as well. ASSESSMENT: the risk is low but the record must not claim the copies match when they do not. THE LF COPY IS THE AUTHORITATIVE ONE FOR RESTORE, because the file is copied into a Cygwin or WSL build tree where the rest of the sources are LF; the CRLF copy would very likely still compile, since C compilers tolerate CRLF, but it is inconsistent with the surrounding tree and would produce spurious differences under any hashing, diffing or git apply step. RESTORE GUIDANCE: prefer the c63ab774 evidence copy, or normalise the 724ee2e9 copy to LF before use, and verify against the normalised sha256 aaf9785b... rather than against either raw byte count. THIS IS THE SAME CRLF HAZARD THE PROGRAMME HAS TRACKED ALL DAY, NOW SURFACING IN THE VERY ARTIFACT INTENDED TO GUARANTEE RECOVERY — which is why the standing rule is to bind identities to NORMALISED content or blob OIDs rather than to raw byte counts.

title: EXTENDED SCAN: 198,151 files — the 67 additional hits are ALL FALSE POSITIVES (host Linux ELF), and the target contamination figure is confirmed unchanged
description: EXTENDED RE-SCAN COMPLETED 2026-09-03, widening from 6,528 extension-filtered binaries to ALL 198,151 FILES under /root/xc with no extension filter, to find anything the first pass missed. RAW RESULT: 668 files containing the pattern, 4,421 encodings, of which 67 files were NOT covered by the earlier scan. THOSE 67 ARE ALL FALSE POSITIVES AND MUST NOT TRIGGER ANY REBUILD. They are HOST LINUX BINARIES, not target artifacts: /root/xc/inst/bin/aarch64-pc-cygwin-as, -ld, -objdump, -ar, -nm, -strip, -dlltool and the rest at 19 encodings each, the same tools mirrored under /root/xc/inst/aarch64-pc-cygwin/bin/, and the GCC build tools under /root/xc/build-gcc2/gcc/ such as xgcc, xg++, cc1-adjacent helpers and collect2 at 2 encodings each. FILE-TYPE EVIDENCE: aarch64-pc-cygwin-as and ld report "ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (SYSV)" and xgcc reports "ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (GNU/Linux)" — these are Linux executables that RUN ON the WSL aarch64 host, whereas the genuine target artifacts are ar archives of PE objects and PE32+ Aarch64 DLLs. THE DECISIVE CONTROL, which settles it beyond argument: I scanned stock unrelated Ubuntu binaries and /usr/bin/python3 CONTAINS 934 OCCURRENCES OF THE SAME PATTERN, with /usr/bin/gcc at 2, while /usr/bin/as and /bin/ls contain none. A stock distribution Python obviously has no Cygwin defect, so the pattern is simply NORMAL AND CORRECT LINUX TLS ACCESS: on Linux/ELF aarch64, tpidr_el0 IS the thread pointer and reading it is the standard idiom. THE DEFECT IS PLATFORM-SPECIFIC, NOT INSTRUCTION-SPECIFIC — the same instruction is correct on Linux and wrong on Windows, which is why the scan must be scoped to TARGET artifacts only. REFINED SCOPING RULE, to be applied to any repeat of this scan: count the encoding ONLY in artifacts destined for Windows, meaning PE/COFF aarch64 objects, ar archives of such objects, and PE images; NEVER in host ELF executables. My original extension filter of .a .o .dll .exe .so .obj .lib achieved this correctly, though partly by accident, since Linux host executables here carry no extension. CONCLUSION: THE TARGET CONTAMINATION FIGURE IS CONFIRMED UNCHANGED at 601 files and 3,829 encodings — bld 298 files/1,676, w-autoload 298/1,676, w-compose 2/236, w-orphans 2/236, w-gendef 1/5 — and inst, w-link, w-implib and w-defects remain CLEAN OF TARGET CONTAMINATION. Nothing was missed by the first pass. IMPORTANT PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE: had the 67 host-binary hits been reported as contamination, someone could have rebuilt or discarded the cross-toolchain itself, which is both wasted effort and actively risky, since inst is the one tree confirmed good and is the foundation everything else depends on.

title: DECISIVE: the Windows SDK DELIBERATELY NORMALISES the ARM64 tag to plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, yielding P19
description:
MEASURED DIRECTLY BY THE COORDINATOR SESSION 2026-09-03 AND IT INVERTS THE NAIVE READING. File: C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Include\10.0.26100.0\um\winnt.h, 876,232 bytes, sha256 8693f0ad4ada355c912d40ca41ce929b480e92291bda2f9227acf56736bffbff. THE COUNT FIRST: word-boundary matching excluding ARM64EC gives SIX occurrences of _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, not seven; the seventh was the ARM64EC substring again, THE SAME SUBSTRING ERROR FOR THE THIRD TIME TODAY. BUT THE COUNT IS NOT MERELY IMPRECISE HERE, IT IS ACTIVELY MISLEADING, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST POSSIBLE VINDICATION OF THE MECHANISM-OVER-COUNTING RULING. Of the six textual occurrences, FIVE ARE PREPROCESSOR PLUMBING and only ONE is a struct declaration: 7099 #pragma push_macro("_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64"), 7100 #undef _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, 7101 #define _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, 7130 typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 {, 7149 #undef, 7150 #pragma pop_macro. THE MECHANISM: lines 7097-7103 are guarded by #if defined(_ARM64_) || defined(_CHPE_X86_ARM64_), and inside that guard line 7101 DEFINES THE IDENTIFIER _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 AS AN OBJECT-LIKE MACRO EXPANDING TO _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. Therefore when line 7130 writes "typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 {" the preprocessor REWRITES THE STRUCT TAG, and the declaration that the compiler actually sees on an ARM64 target is "typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT { ... } DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64, *PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64;". Line 7147, inside the same arch guard, then does "typedef DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, *PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT;", and 7149-7150 undef and pop_macro so the rewrite does not leak. NET RESULT ON ARM64: PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT RESOLVES TO struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT *, SO MICROSOFT AUTHORITATIVE SDK MANGLES TO P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, NOT P25. THE NUMBER OF STRUCT DECLARATIONS THAT SURVIVE AS _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 ON AN ARM64 TARGET IS ZERO. CONSEQUENCE, WHICH INVERTS THE EARLIER INFERENCE: it is NOT the case that the authoritative Microsoft header makes P25-style naming the norm and v12.0.0 the outlier. THE OPPOSITE IS TRUE. Microsoft DELIBERATELY NORMALISES the ARM64 tag to the plain name, so w32api v12.0.0 (plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, P19) AGREES WITH MICROSOFT, while CLANGARM64 and mingw-w64 master (genuine _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 tag aliased at 2496 and 2481 respectively, P25) ARE THE DIVERGENCE FROM MICROSOFT. On non-ARM64 targets the 7097 guard is false, so no macro rewrite happens and _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 exists as a genuinely distinct cross-architecture type — which is exactly why a naive textual grep on a non-ARM64 machine reports its presence and misleads. NOTHING HERE CHANGES THE FIX REQUIREMENT: the correct name still varies BY HEADER SET, so the port must still be VERSION-ROBUST rather than hard-coding either spelling. What changes is which spelling is the Microsoft-authoritative one, and the false comment in exception.h:16-18 turns out to be closer to Microsoft behaviour than to mingw-w64 behaviour while still being wrong as a universal.

COORDINATOR INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED THIS REVERSAL RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT, 2026-09-03, reading the SDK region verbatim and confirming 7097, 7099, 7100, 7101, 7103, 7130, 7149 and 7150 exactly as reported, and noting that the push_macro/pop_macro bracketing SHOWS THE CONTAINMENT IS DELIBERATE. THE UPSTREAM FRAMING IS STRUCK, NOT MERELY AMENDED: the coordinator had told the programme owner that the SDK "defines it seven times, so version-robustness is the behaviour of the authoritative Microsoft header", and has corrected that upstream. THE TRUTH IS THE OPPOSITE — MICROSOFT DELIBERATELY NORMALISES TO THE PLAIN TAG, so w32api v12.0.0 AGREES with Microsoft while CLANGARM64 and mingw-w64 master are THE DIVERGENCE. Note for the record that the incorrect framing was never written into this tracker; the only SDK record ever created here is this one, which carried the corrected account from the outset. A FOURTH SUBSTRING SOURCE identified by the coordinator: line 7115 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_NONVOLREG_ARM64, which also contains the ARM64 token and would inflate a naive grep further. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, STATED EXPLICITLY SO NOBODY OVER-CORRECTS: THE FIX REQUIREMENT IS UNCHANGED. The mangled name still varies BY HEADER SET, so it must still be DERIVED rather than hard-coded, and a token swap to P19 is still wrong. ONLY THE QUESTION OF WHICH SPELLING IS AUTHORITATIVE FLIPS. Related observation worth keeping: the false comment at exception.h:16-18 turns out to be CLOSER TO MICROSOFT ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR THAN TO MINGW-W64 BEHAVIOUR while STILL BEING WRONG AS A UNIVERSAL — A COMMENT CAN BE ACCIDENTALLY NEAR-RIGHT AND STILL DANGEROUS, BECAUSE IT ASSERTS A UNIVERSALITY IT NEVER ESTABLISHED. title: Resolving intended aarch64 Cygwin data model
description: RESOLVED BY EVIDENCE: LP64. Answered 2026-09-03 by BUILDING the aarch64-pc-cygwin GCC target and measuring predefines and codegen, not by reading config fragments. Position B (LLP64) NEVER EXISTED AS AN ARTIFACT: llp64 is a placeholder token the compiler rejects and configure discards, and upstream removed the lines entirely. STRUCTURAL REASON IT COULD NEVER HAVE EXISTED: newlib sys/_types.h, the header Cygwin actually uses, defines _off_t, __blkcnt_t, __blksize_t, _ssize_t, time_t, _fpos_t and clock_t in terms of bare long, and __ino_t/__mode_t as unsigned long; under a 32-bit long these are not work items but a SILENT PLATFORM-WIDE ABI BREAK — 2GB file ceiling, Y2038 in time_t, truncated inode numbers and block counts, ssize_t narrower than size_t. Nothing in winsup is conditioned for that. Cygwin documented architecture-neutral contract, verbatim in our own tree at winsup/doc/gcc.xml:37-46: "While the Mingw and Microsoft compilers use the LLP64 data model, Cygwin compilers use the LP64 data model, just like Linux." No LLP64 branch exists anywhere in winsup; winsup/utils/getconf.c selects between exactly two models on __LP64__ and an LLP64 ARM64 Cygwin would make getconf report ILP32. Windows-on-ARM-Experiments/newlib-cygwin CI builds and make checks the real Cygwin DLL with --target=aarch64-pc-cygwin on windows-11-arm and its failure triage (issue #303) lists signal/cygserver/pointer-validation failures and NOT ONE type-size failure, which a 32-bit long would produce everywhere. CONSEQUENCE: clang aarch64-pc-cygwin __SIZEOF_LONG__=4 is conclusively A CLANG DEFECT, not a competing data model. OWNER RATIFICATION STILL OUTSTANDING — this records decisive evidence, NOT a granted decision; no session_start authority is created by it.

title: LESSON: an artifact name is a DISCOVERY AFFORDANCE, and misleading naming is itself a hazard
description: GENERAL LESSON recorded 2026-09-03, and it is DISTINCT FROM the content hazard already closed. THE SPECIFIC TRAP: both CRLF copies of longdouble.c live in the bundle named arm64-port-backup-2026-09-02 — THE ARTIFACT WHOSE NAME SAYS IT IS THE PORT BACKUP — while the BYTE-EXACT copy sits under a session named for a LINK ATTEMPT (c63ab774). A successor reaching for the thing labelled "port backup" therefore gets the NON-BYTE-EXACT copy, entirely reasonably. Content survives either way; byte-exactness does not. THE GENERAL FORM: AN ARTIFACT NAME IS A DISCOVERY AFFORDANCE, AND WHEN THE AUTHORITATIVE COPY LIVES SOMEWHERE LESS OBVIOUSLY NAMED, THE NAMING ITSELF BECOMES A HAZARD THAT DOCUMENTATION MUST ACTIVELY COUNTERACT. It is not enough for the authoritative copy to exist and be correct; it must be REACHABLE BY THE SEARCH A SUCCESSOR WILL ACTUALLY PERFORM, which is usually "find the thing whose name matches what I want". WHERE THIS DIFFERS FROM ORDINARY DOCUMENTATION DEBT: the misleading name actively competes with the correct pointer, so a note buried in one README is insufficient — the counteracting instruction must sit AT THE POINT OF DISCOVERY, i.e. in the misleadingly-named artifact itself. That is why the fix was to amend BOTH backup READMEs rather than only the authoritative one. RELATED PRIOR INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE: my own failed search for clang, and the heartbeat failed search for winnt.h, both looked in the plausibly-named place (system installs) rather than the actual one (session state).

title: LESSON: a scratch edit carrying a confident universal justification is more dangerous than an obviously-temporary one
description: GENERALISED LESSON recorded 2026-09-03, and it reaches well beyond this case. A SCRATCH EDIT THAT CARRIES A CONFIDENT UNIVERSAL JUSTIFICATION IS MORE DANGEROUS THAN AN OBVIOUSLY-TEMPORARY ONE. AN UNLABELLED HACK GETS CAUGHT IN REVIEW; A HACK WITH AN AUTHORITATIVE COMMENT GETS RATIFIED BY IT. CONCRETE INSTANCE: a throwaway diagnostic edit hard-coded P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT into the build tree, which by itself would be caught, but it sits under exception.h:16-18 asserting "plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT on every architecture — there is no _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64". That assertion is FALSE as a universal, yet it reads as settled design and would licence a future reader to propagate the assumption. Worse, cygtls.h:365 still claims the OPPOSITE while the code three lines below emits P19, so the file contradicts itself. PRACTICAL RULE: when making a temporary or diagnostic edit, LABEL IT AS TEMPORARY AND SCOPE-LIMITED; never justify it with a confident universal claim about the platform. If a universal claim is genuinely warranted it must be verified across every header set or toolchain in use, which in this programme means at minimum CLANGARM64, released w32api v12.0.0 and mingw-w64 master — three sets that DEMONSTRABLY DISAGREE.

title: LESSON: I verify countable claims and wave through interpretive ones
description: SELF-DIAGNOSED MEASUREMENT-ERROR PATTERN, recorded 2026-09-03 in the same family as the git status staleness, the substring process filter, the collapsed patch artifact and the echoed-string false corroboration. THE ASYMMETRY: I verified every COUNTABLE claim in the link report — sigfe.s at literally 0 bytes, scripts/gendef:24 read directly rather than trusted from the summary, 271 objects counted with find, both archives confirmed as pe-aarch64-little — AND WAVED THROUGH THE INTERPRETIVE ONE, recording "a one-token fix in each of two files" without testing it. WHY IT HAPPENS, and this is the useful part: COUNTS FEEL CHECKABLE SO THEY GET CHECKED, WHILE CHARACTERISATIONS LIKE "one-token fix", "mechanical", "cosmetic only" or "source-non-causal" SLIDE PAST BECAUSE THEY READ AS SUMMARY RATHER THAN AS CLAIM. They are claims, and they are usually the ones that drive decisions. PRACTICAL RULE: treat every characterisation of SCOPE, DIFFICULTY or CAUSE as a claim requiring the same verification as a number. For "one-token fix" specifically, the test is trivial and I skipped it: ask what else must be true for the single token to be correct, which here would immediately have surfaced that the correct token differs by header set. REPORTED RESULT FROM 200edc20, NOT VERIFIED BY ME AND DELIBERATELY NOT VERIFIED because I am stood down from proactive validation: autoload.o now assembles; 192 of 192 autoload undefined references eliminated; total undefined 196 to 4; NO DLL PRODUCED, since sigfe symbols remain missing. Three fixes claimed, all in aarch64 blocks of autoload.cc: .align to .balign, on the grounds that AArch64 GAS treats .align N as 2^N bytes so .align 16 requested 65536-byte alignment and was fatal for PE; removal of .if (2b - name) % 8 because AArch64 GAS cannot evaluate label-difference expressions in .if for PE/COFF, replaced by .balign 8; and no other changes, the existing thunk code being already correct. THE x18 RULE HELD AND WAS EXPLICITLY REPORTED: "x18: never written. Only x16/x17 used as scratch." That binding rule was recorded specifically so it would survive into the trampoline work, and it did. DISCLOSED RESIDUAL RISK FROM THAT SESSION, WORTH CARRYING: the thunk saves x0-x8 and x30, 80 bytes, but DOES NOT SAVE v0-v7, the SIMD and floating-point argument registers. It notes this mirrors the x86_64 thunk which does not save xmm0-xmm3, and assesses the risk as low because most Win32 APIs take integer arguments, but ANY AUTOLOADED FUNCTION WITH FLOAT OR DOUBLE PARAMETERS COULD CORRUPT ON FIRST CALL. It recommends an audit in follow-up. RESIDUAL FAILURES IT REPORTS AS SIBLING SCOPE: 4 undefined (_sigbe, sigdelayed, _sigdelayed_end, _sigfe_malloc), roughly 1013 cannot-export all _sigfe_*, and 8 or more IMAGE_REL_ARM64_PAGEOFFSET_12L relocation truncation errors in exceptions.o attributed to import library alignment. title: MEASURED BY COMPILER: three-variant mangling probe independently reproduced, including Variant C
description: INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY THE COORDINATOR SESSION 2026-09-03 USING A REAL COMPILER, not argued from the ABI rule. Compiler: clang++ 22.1.8 at C:\Users\crutkasLocal\.copilot\session-state\aabca41f-e845-47dd-97cd-bc99428bc7d4\files\arm64-local-workload\toolchain-root\clangarm64\bin\clang++.exe, built from MINGW-packages 6e4e79c2f86eeb534e324e583f2057dc9fd5ecab, default target aarch64-w64-windows-gnu, invoked with --target=aarch64-w64-mingw32 -S so the emitted assembly could be read directly. THIS IS THE SAME COMPILER FAMILY THAT WOULD BUILD THIS RUNTIME. Each variant declared the identical member function int exception::myfault(_EXCEPTION_RECORD*, void*, _CONTEXT*, PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT) and differed ONLY in how PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT was constructed. RESULTS, read from the generated assembly: VARIANT A, plain "struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT" with a direct pointer typedef, the w32api v12.0.0 shape, produced _ZN9exception7myfaultEP17_EXCEPTION_RECORDPvP8_CONTEXTP19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. VARIANT B, a genuine "typedef struct _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 {...} DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64" then aliased to DISPATCHER_CONTEXT and PDISPATCHER_CONTEXT, which is the CLANGARM64 and mingw-w64-master shape, produced ...P25_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64. VARIANT C, THE DECISIVE ONE, reproduced the Microsoft sequence — #define _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, then the ARM64-NAMED typedef whose underlying TAG is thereby normalised, then #undef — and produced ...P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. SO AN ARM64-NAMED TYPEDEF WHOSE TAG HAS BEEN NORMALISED MANGLES TO P19, WHICH IS EXACTLY THE INFERENCE BOTH PARTIES ORIGINALLY GOT BACKWARDS, NOW SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT. EPISTEMIC EFFECT ON THE THREE-TIER CHAIN: tier 2, what each construction mangles to, is now INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED BY COMPILER for ALL THREE constructions rather than derived from the Itanium ABI rule. Tier 1, which construction each header set uses, remains measured from header text. THE ONLY REMAINING INFERENTIAL STEP IS THE COMPOSITION of tiers 1 and 2 — that each named header set, when actually compiled, uses the construction read from its text — and that leap is now materially smaller, though still not zero, since winnt.h itself was compiled for no set. The w32api v12.0.0 row remains the only one confirmed end-to-end by a real exceptions.o from real headers. NOTHING ABOUT THE FIX REQUIREMENT CHANGES: two header sets in active use still produce P25, so version-robustness remains mandatory and no token swap is safe in either direction.
