title: MILESTONE: a usable aarch64-pc-cygwin cross exists and compiled 254 real runtime objects
description:
CORRECTED AND EXPANDED 2026-09-03 from session 1e64365a own final report, with the two load-bearing claims INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AT SOURCE by the coordinator session. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO WHAT I PREVIOUSLY RECORDED: the figure "254 real runtime objects with 8 distinct errors remaining" WAS A CONFLATION and corresponds to NO SINGLE CONFIGURATION. It paired a row-3 object count with a row-4 error count. THE TRUE PROGRESSION, from the session own table, out of 310 objects: (1) w32api master, no fixes = 116 objects / 314 error lines; (2) + _WIN64 fix = 116 / 285; (3) + released w32api v12.0.0 = 254 / 15; (4) + 3 target-detection fixes = 261 / 8; (5) warnings non-fatal = 265 / 3. FINAL STATE IS 265 OF 310 OBJECTS, 85 PERCENT, WITH 3 ERRORS. At row 5 the ONLY hard compile error left is "fatal error: new: No such file or directory", i.e. libstdc++ headers were never installed — TOOLCHAIN COMPLETENESS, NOT A PORT GAP. ROOT CAUSE, VERIFIED VERBATIM AT SOURCE BY ME: mingw-w64-headers/crt/_cygwin.h is 36 lines and lines 32-34 read exactly "#ifdef __x86_64__ / #define _WIN64 / #endif", with the preceding comment explaining that _WIN64 is normally set by the compiler specs and is therefore set here. __x86_64__ is UNDEFINED on aarch64-pc-cygwin, so _WIN64 is never set, so basetsd.h silently takes its 32-BIT branch and UINT_PTR, INT_PTR, LONG_PTR, ULONG_PTR, SOCKET and DWORD_PTR all become 32-bit. That produces a flood of pointer-truncation errors THAT LOOK EXACTLY LIKE ARM64 PORT DEFECTS AND ARE NOT. One-line fix: #if defined(__x86_64__) || defined(__aarch64__). This is a genuine upstream mingw-w64 defect affecting ANY non-x86_64 64-bit Cygwin target. DECISIVE RESULT FOR THE 11 SITES: they COMPILE CLEAN UNDER LP64 — every pointer-width error vanished the instant _WIN64 was correct, and a direct probe compiled clean asserting sizeof(UINT_PTR)==8 && sizeof(void*)==8 && sizeof(long)==8 against real <w32api/windows.h>. LEAVING THEM UNPATCHED WAS CORRECT, and this converts the "estimated remaining work: zero" from an INFERENCE into a MEASURED RESULT. The sealed port applied cleanly (29 files / 785 insertions plus math/aarch64/longdouble.c copied separately) to a scratch clone at d890a845. WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING was C++: winsup/cygwin is overwhelmingly .cc and a C-only cross cannot touch it; reconfiguring with --enable-languages=c,c++ and make all-gcc took 3m04s and yielded cc1plus and aarch64-pc-cygwin-g++ WITHOUT needing a target libc, after which winsup/configure --host=aarch64-pc-cygwin SUCCEEDED with target_cpu=aarch64. Binutils was never the problem and was NOT rebuilt: the existing 2.44.50 at /root/xc/inst already supports aarch64pe/arm64pe emulations and pe-aarch64-little/pei-aarch64-little BFD targets with dlltool and windres. mingw-w64 w32api configures and installs cleanly for --host=aarch64-pc-cygwin (1635 headers); newlib/configure --host=aarch64-pc-cygwin SUCCEEDS since configure.host already carries aarch64*) machine_dir=aarch64 and *-*-cygwin*, and it correctly detects _LDBL_EQ_DBL 1 for Windows ARM64. Constraints honoured: no commits, pushes, refs, PRs, CI, upstream submission or contributor contact; crutkas-refactored-carnival NEVER OPENED, backup read read-only; nothing under arm64-vnext/continuity/; all work in a WSL scratch clone; its own worktree has zero modifications.

FIGURE PRECISION 2026-09-03 — THIS CORRECTS THE CORRECTION, and it changes what the sealed port is credited with. The three target-detection fixes behind rows 4 and 5 (fabsl.c, cygwin.sc.in, MALLOC_ALIGNMENT) are THROWAWAY DIAGNOSTICS made in the WSL scratch clone ONLY to prove the remaining failures were source-side rather than toolchain. They are NOT proposed patches and are NOT committed anywhere. THEREFORE: THE SEALED PORT AS-IS REACHES ROW 3 — 254 OF 310 OBJECTS WITH 15 ERRORS. Rows 4 (261/8) and 5 (265/3) describe what it WOULD reach ONCE THOSE THREE FIXES ARE DONE PROPERLY. Any citation of "265/310, 85 percent" MUST carry the qualifier "achievable once three further fixes land"; unqualified it overstates the sealed port. This is the SECOND figure error in this thread — first the row-3/row-4 conflation, now the missing conditional qualifier — and in both cases THE FIVE-ROW LABELLED TABLE IS WHAT MADE THE ERROR DETECTABLE.

title: Scoping clang aarch64 cygwin identity defect
description:
DONE, reported by session d5162ce1 and INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED FROM UPSTREAM SOURCE by the coordinator. (a) DEFECT IS WORSE THAN RECORDED AND THE FRAMING CHANGES: aarch64-pc-cygwin does not merely LACK identity, it POSITIVELY CLAIMS TO BE AN MSVC ARM64 TARGET by defining _M_ARM64=1, and inherits TargetCXXABI::Microsoft C++ mangling with it. Correct framing is a CONTRADICTORY identity, not an absent one. COORDINATOR VERIFICATION LIMIT: could NOT reproduce empirically because NO clang exists on this host and C:\msys64 is absent, so the live macro dump remains UNVERIFIED BY ME; however the causal chain is CONFIRMED CONCLUSIVELY FROM UPSTREAM SOURCE. (c) MECHANISM CONFIRMED VERBATIM at clang/lib/Basic/Targets.cpp:185-192 on llvm-project main: case Triple::Win32 switches on environment, case GNU returns MinGWARM64TargetInfo, then "case MSVC: default: // Assume MSVC for unknown environments" returns MicrosoftARM64TargetInfo. Cygnus is not handled so it falls to that default. _M_ARM64 is emitted at clang/lib/Basic/Targets/AArch64.cpp:1839, only two sites in the file (1837 _M_ARM64EC, 1839 _M_ARM64), inside the Microsoft path. The fingerprint claim is therefore structurally proven even without running clang. PEER-ARCH ASYMMETRY CONFIRMED: exactly three Triple::Cygnus cases exist upstream, at Targets.cpp:244 (ARM), :611 (x86-32) and :673 (x86-64); AArch64 IS THE ONLY ARCH MISSING ONE. (b) UPSTREAM NOT FIXED, NOT REPORTED, NOT IN FLIGHT: zero Cygwin mentions anywhere in AArch64.cpp, confirming no CygwinARM64TargetInfo; session also found none on release/21.x or release/22.x, zero commit-search hits for "cygwin aarch64", and the only issue hit PR #134494 concerns BUILDING LLVM on x86_64 Cygwin and is unrelated, closed and unmerged. Driver is ALREADY aarch64-Cygwin-aware (Driver.cpp:7319 maps Cygnus to toolchains::Cygwin for all arches; Cygwin.cpp:53 and :159-165 enumerate Triple::aarch64 and emit -m arm64pe), so clang DRIVES A CYGWIN/GNU TOOLCHAIN WHILE THE FRONTEND DESCRIBES AN MSVC TARGET: a self-contained internal inconsistency, not a feature request. (d) PATCH VERIFIED BY COORDINATOR: 3662 bytes, sha256 934c0a209c7c3a9120ea800833edb71c2bea5a37b2d04acb52e4ff299605ec7b, 76 physical lines so NOT collapsed by the known PowerShell single-line corruption hazard, 3 diff headers touching exactly clang/lib/Basic/Targets.cpp, clang/lib/Basic/Targets/AArch64.cpp and clang/lib/Basic/Targets/AArch64.h, 43 insertions and 0 deletions exactly as claimed. Adds case Triple::Cygnus plus CygwinARM64TargetInfo defining __CYGWIN__, addCygMingDefines, DefineStd(unix) and _GNU_SOURCE for C++ only, and touches TheCXXABI. Session reports it applies cleanly to pristine main via git apply --check and type-checks including override signature match. GUARDRAIL 4 HONOURED AND COORDINATOR-CONFIRMED: the patch contains NO SIZEOF_LONG line and no multilib change; base class is deliberately WindowsARM64TargetInfo so every width, alignment and the data layout string stay bit-for-bit identical. __SIZEOF_LONG__ stays 4. A NO-CHANGE choice, explicitly NOT an LLP64 endorsement. Net effect: gains __CYGWIN__, __unix__, __declspec and _GNU_SOURCE; loses _M_ARM64; C++ mangling moves Microsoft to Itanium; no width changes. TENSION FLAGGED HONESTLY BY THE SESSION RATHER THAN SILENTLY RESOLVED: CygwinX86_64TargetInfo and CygwinARMTargetInfo derive from the PLAIN non-Windows arch target, which is precisely what gives x86_64 Cygwin both LP64 and the absence of _WIN32; mirroring that shape would flip __SIZEOF_LONG__ to 8 and thereby ANSWER IOU ITEM 8. It deliberately did NOT do that. Left open: (1) data model; (2) _WIN32/_WIN64, which x86_64 Cygwin omits and PR #134494 called erroneous, but removal requires changing the base class so it is coupled to (1); (3) __CYGWIN64__ omitted as it denotes the LP64 flavour; (4) WIntType; (5) TheCXXABI to GenericAArch64, marked in-code as a separable sub-fix droppable on its own. (e) BUILD DEFERRED ON SESSION RECOMMENDATION AND NOT STARTED: neither cmake nor ninja is on PATH and none ships in the VS2022 BuildTools install; a clang-only Release build would cost roughly 2.5-4h and 30GB and would only confirm the AFTER state, since the BEFORE state is already pinned by the _M_ARM64 fingerprint. All four sealed artifacts independently re-hashed and PASS against the session own SHA256SUMS.txt manifest: aarch64-cygwin-identity.diff 3662 bytes 934c0a209c7c3a9120ea800833edb71c2bea5a37b2d04acb52e4ff299605ec7b (UNCHANGED from the interim verification); FINDINGS.md 13330 bytes 07288c37945465af003fc0c66466056d43813ae1147e2bd97ce6e9a8fa1f65a5 (CHANGED — SUPERSEDES the earlier f7b3c764a68c7a6f7d7cf0fb8c698cc92eaeaff817cd32f6b8fd058558be1bc5, which is now STALE and must not be cited); mangle-test.cpp 76 bytes be9b01efb9c35f53cfab85225e14093b21f168457ceb143062ecc17f83eb6ca6 (NEW); syntax-harness.cpp 2824 bytes 79bb8c966f4855f967681480dc87f1d89392b8836222ef9aced456c03b76887a (UNCHANGED). (1) The C++ mangling claim was UNDERSTATED by the session: it had asserted the target "inherits" Microsoft mangling, whereas testing EMISSION rather than assuming it shows aarch64-pc-cygwin ACTUALLY EMITS Microsoft-mangled C++ symbols today. title: Verifying PR10 CI failure attribution
description: DONE. VERIFIED, AND THE PRIOR CLASSIFICATION IS CORRECTED. Mechanism confirmed accurate against the current log, not inherited: configure reports "checking for makeinfo... no", then 4 minutes later MAKEINFO doc/bfd.info fails with "makeinfo: command not found", make error 127, makepkg exit 4, in job 99705967208 step 14. BUT the attached classification "source-non-causal, monitor only, outside our control" was WRONG. It is a one-line defect in OUR OWN workflow file and the fix already exists in this repository. ATTRIBUTION (b) PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE ON main, NOT CAUSED BY PR #10, verified independently by the coordinator: PR #10 changes 59 files, ALL under arm64-vnext/continuity/**, with ZERO files under .github/ or packages/ (coordinator measured 59 where the triage session said 58; the zero-CI-files fact is unchanged and decisive). origin/main .github/workflows/mingw-cross-toolchain.yml binutils block has NO dependencies: line at all (coordinator confirmed HasDependenciesLine=0), so install-dependencies.sh receives an empty extra-deps string and PR #10 inherits it verbatim. An unrelated branch fails byte-identically, as does every run of this workflow since 2026-08-27 across four branches. DECISIVE A/B: of 13 workflow runs exactly one succeeded, run 31730036493 on 2026-08-13 on branch crutkas-harden-arm64-bootstrap (PR #1), which is the only branch carrying dependencies: texinfo; its log shows "installing texinfo..." then "checking for makeinfo... makeinfo" and binutils passed. So the fix was written, validated green, and never landed on main; every branch cut from main since reproduces the failure. ROOT MECHANISM: makepkg --syncdeps installs only the PKGBUILD makedepends, which lack texinfo, and neither base-devel nor the autotools group provides it; the string texinfo never appears in either install transaction in the failing log. MINIMAL FIX for application under SEPARATE authority: add "dependencies: texinfo" to the with: block of job mingw-w64-cross-mingwarm64-binutils in .github/workflows/mingw-cross-toolchain.yml, exactly as PR #1 has and proven green. LATENT GAP FLAGGED: native mingw-w64-binutils in mingw-native-toolchain.yml likewise passes no texinfo and its MINGW-packages PKGBUILD makedepends also lack it. QUEUE/TIMEOUT IS SEPARATE (d): the 7 cancelled jobs are all MinGW native toolchain jobs on self-hosted labels Windows,ARM64,MSYS2, cancelled after exactly 24h having never been picked up, i.e. a missing or offline self-hosted ARM64 runner; the binutils job by contrast ran on hosted windows-latest and genuinely compiled 11m2s before a real build error. title: STANDING RULE: continuity line-ending conventions are per-file, not global
description: Refined 2026-09-03 after a full audit. The continuity directory ships .gitattributes containing "* -text", so git performs NO line-ending conversion and WORKTREE BYTES ARE AUTHORITATIVE AND EQUAL BLOB BYTES. SHA256SUMS records are therefore plain sha256 of worktree bytes — confirmed empirically 59/60 matched worktree bytes while ZERO matched LF-normalized or git-blob-header hashing. CRITICAL REFINEMENT to my earlier over-broad rule "continuity files are literal CRLF": that is true of the state/*.md files (plan.md measured CRLF=100, BareLF=0) but NOT of SHA256SUMS itself, whose committed blob has ALWAYS been LF-only (HEAD blob CRLF=0, BareLF=58; worktree now 60 records, still LF). Do NOT "fix" SHA256SUMS to CRLF; that would be a corruption, not a repair. Verify per-file against the committed blob rather than assuming a single global convention.

title: STANDING RULE: do not concede to a contradiction until it is verified, any more than you defend wording
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03, the corollary to the rule that neither party should defend wording once evidence points elsewhere. THE ADDITION: DO NOT CONCEDE TO A CONTRADICTION EITHER, UNTIL IT IS VERIFIED. The coordinator nearly retracted a CORRECT finding out of deference to a confident contradicting report from the heartbeat context, and only avoided it by re-running the check at the exact path. Deference to confidence is the mirror image of attachment to wording, and it fails in the same way: both substitute a social signal for evidence. THE PRACTICAL TEST IS SYMMETRIC — when challenged, re-measure; when challenging, measure first. Note the specific asymmetry that makes negative claims dangerous: an assertion that something EXISTS carries its own evidence (a path, a hash, a line number), whereas an assertion that something DOES NOT EXIST carries none, and is indistinguishable from having looked in the wrong place. Require the searched paths before accepting any negative.

title: STANDING RULE (SHARPENED): process snapshots are valid only for long-running compile phases
description: SHARPENED STANDING RULE, 2026-09-03, after the SECOND process-count misread in one day. Incident one: 40 stale git fsmonitor--daemon instances from 2026-08-31 were read as active compilers because the filter matched the substring "git". Incident two: a further process-count misread of the same class. THE RULE: PROCESS SNAPSHOTS ARE VALID ONLY FOR LONG-RUNNING COMPILE PHASES. They are USELESS for short-lived link and analysis steps, which begin and end between samples, and they are BLIND ACROSS THE WSL BOUNDARY because Windows-side process counts CANNOT SEE GUEST PROCESSES. CHECK ARTIFACTS INSTEAD — logs, output files, and the script step sequence — before inferring activity. Filter on actual compiler executable names (cc1, cc1plus, as, ld, collect2) rather than substrings that unrelated tooling also matches. NOTED AS A SHARED LESSON, NOT A PERSONAL ONE: the coordinator made the same class of error earlier with the ABI session and had to retract it. This belongs to the same family as the git-status staleness that caused the NUL.exe misreport and the unvalidated-patch-artifact hazard: TRUSTING A SINGLE CONVENIENCE SIGNAL INSTEAD OF PROBING THE ACTUAL OBJECT.

title: STANDING RULE: report multi-configuration results as the full labelled progression, never a single headline number
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03 after TWO figure errors in one thread on the same result. Error one: "254 objects / 8 errors" conflated a row-3 object count with a row-4 error count, a pairing matching NO configuration. Error two: "265/310, 85 percent" omitted the qualifier that rows 4 and 5 depend on three throwaway diagnostic fixes that are not committed and not proposed, so the sealed port as-is actually reaches only row 3 at 254/15. THE RULE: MULTI-CONFIGURATION RESULTS MUST ALWAYS BE REPORTED AS THE FULL LABELLED PROGRESSION, NEVER AS A SINGLE HEADLINE NUMBER. Each row must name its configuration and state whether the changes it depends on are committed, proposed, or throwaway diagnostics. RATIONALE THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN BOOKKEEPING: in both incidents it was the five-row table itself that made the error detectable — a single headline figure would have propagated silently and become programme belief. Prefer publishing the table even when it is more verbose than the ask.

title: STANDING RULE: reseal in the same turn as the edit and replay in full
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03 after I found and self-reported genuine unsealed drift on the IOU list. RESEAL IMMEDIATELY AFTER EVERY CONTINUITY EDIT, in the SAME turn, never deferred. Then run a FULL replay of every SHA256SUMS record rather than trusting that only the touched record changed — the full replay is the check that catches what memory does not. The drift that prompted this went undetected precisely because nothing had re-run a complete verification since the edit. An integrity system only works if the participants report their own drift, so self-reported seal failures are to be recorded prominently, not quietly repaired.

title: STANDING RULE: label measured versus derived columns; do not present a mixed table at uniform confidence
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03, taken from the honesty boundary that session c63ab774 applied to its own census and that the coordinator asked me to adopt. IN THE DISPATCHER_CONTEXT CENSUS, THE HEADER-TEXT FACTS ARE MEASURED — byte counts, sha256 values, the presence or absence of a normalising #define, and the line numbers of each declaration and guard, all of which I read directly from the files. THE "MANGLES TO P19 OR P25" COLUMN IS DERIVED, inferred from the Itanium ABI rule that C++ mangling uses the underlying struct tag rather than the typedef name. ONLY THE w32api v12.0.0 ROW HAS BEEN EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED, by a real exceptions.o observed to define ...P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT. THE OTHER FOUR ROWS ARE SOUND DERIVATIONS BUT HAVE NOT BEEN COMPILED. THE RULE: WHEN A TABLE MIXES MEASURED AND DERIVED COLUMNS, LABEL THEM, AND DO NOT PRESENT ALL ROWS AT UNIFORM CONFIDENCE. This matters here because the derivation is exactly the step that the whole episode showed can be got wrong: the naive derivation from occurrence counts inverted the answer, and only reading the preprocessor behaviour corrected it. A derivation that is currently believed sound deserves to be labelled as a derivation precisely BECAUSE the previous derivation was wrong.

title: STANDING RULE: substring matching on identifiers is unsafe wherever a longer identifier shares the prefix
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03 after the SAME failure occurred twice in one day on two different kinds of name. INSTANCE ONE, process names: a filter matching the substring "git" counted 40 stale git-fsmonitor--daemon processes as active compilers. INSTANCE TWO, C identifiers: a count of "2 occurrences of _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64" in the CLANGARM64 winnt.h was a SUBSTRING count — the second hit at line 3126 is _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64EC, A DIFFERENT STRUCT that merely shares the prefix. One genuine occurrence, one artifact. THE RULE: SUBSTRING MATCHING ON IDENTIFIERS IS UNSAFE WHEREVER A LONGER IDENTIFIER SHARES THE PREFIX — ARM64 versus ARM64EC, git versus git-fsmonitor. MATCH ON TOKEN BOUNDARIES OR VERIFY EACH HIT INDIVIDUALLY. Note the coordinator recorded this as their own error and observed they made it WHILE CATALOGUING THAT EXACT CLASS, which is worth remembering: knowing about a failure mode does not prevent committing it, so the mitigation must be a mechanical habit (word-boundary regex, per-hit inspection) rather than vigilance.

title: STANDING RULE: a rule derived from one artifact class must be tested before applying to another
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03 after the SECOND over-broad generalisation in a single day. Case one, the coordinator: core.autocrlf=false was correct for git archive (which EXPORTS bytes) and was wrongly generalised to git diff (which COMPARES against the index), producing a degenerate whole-file patch of 13,736/13,002 instead of the true 785/51. Case two, mine: "continuity files are literal CRLF" was correct for state/*.md and was wrongly generalised to SHA256SUMS, which is LF BY DESIGN. Empirical proof of the correct per-file convention: .gitattributes is "* -text" so git performs NO conversion and worktree bytes equal blob bytes; 59 of 60 records matched worktree-byte hashing while ZERO matched LF-normalized or git-blob-header hashing; the SHA256SUMS HEAD blob measured 0 CRLF / 58 bare LF whereas plan.md measured 100 CRLF / 0 bare LF. "Fixing" the sums file to CRLF would have been CORRUPTION PRESENTED AS REPAIR. THE RULE: before applying a convention learned on one artifact class to another, TEST IT against the second class empirically. Prefer measuring the committed blob over assuming a single global convention.

title: STANDING RULE: verify resulting state after any mutation that appears to fail
description: Standing rule adopted 2026-09-03 after I misreported the NUL.exe deletion. A FAILED-LOOKING OPERATION IS NOT PROOF OF NO EFFECT. With Windows reserved names the error can arrive after the change has taken, and a status command run immediately afterwards can report stale state. ALWAYS RE-PROBE THE ACTUAL OBJECT after a mutation that appears to fail, using a direct filesystem or authoritative check rather than a convenience wrapper, and prefer MORE THAN ONE independent probe. Corollary and the sharper half of the lesson: CHECK PROVENANCE BEFORE DELETING, NOT AFTER. Reconsidering on evidence was right; acting on the assumption first was the error. Applies to any destructive or state-changing operation, not just deletes.

title: ANSWERED s48: the sealed patch REFERENCES longdouble.c without CREATING it — mechanism, not assertion
description: ANSWERED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR SESSION 2026-09-03 against the sealed arm64-port.patch (49,823 bytes, sha256 e2068db8de17df27cedc3e1fe61c1f182fac1347df22da351e2ada75e130089f). A grep for "longdouble" in the patch DOES match, which superficially looks like a contradiction of the standing restore warning, BUT THERE IS EXACTLY ONE MENTION AND IT IS NOT A FILE CREATION. Line 187 is "+\tmath/aarch64/longdouble.c", an entry added to Makefile.am. VERIFIED: the number of "diff --git" headers naming longdouble is ZERO. SO THE PATCH REFERENCES THE FILE WITHOUT CREATING IT. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOW A MECHANISM RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION: applying the sealed patch alone yields a Makefile.am that points at a NONEXISTENT FILE, and the tree therefore fails at LINK with the long double symbols missing — far from the apparent cause. That is precisely why the separate copy step exists, and a successor now knows WHY rather than merely being instructed to do it. THE SAME CHECK INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMED THE SEALED PORT SHAPE BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY QUOTATION: 29 diff --git headers, 785 insertions, 51 deletions — exactly the recorded 29 files / 785 / 51. ALSO MEASURED: the patch contains ZERO CR BYTES, i.e. it is pure LF despite living on NTFS under a global core.autocrlf=true. THAT IS NOT LUCK — it is the direct result of writing the artifact with "git diff --output=<file>" INSTEAD OF THROUGH A SHELL PIPELINE, a deliberate choice made in response to the earlier collapsed-patch failure, and it is the reason this verification passed rather than uncovering a disaster. STAND DOWN: s48 is answered and requires no further work.

title: SWEEP DONE: two architectural-fact comments confirmed WRONG in the shared tree, one further candidate flagged unverified
description: SWEPT 2026-09-03 at coordinator request, searching /root/xc/runtime/winsup/cygwin for comments asserting architectural facts about Windows ARM64. THE PATTERN, NOW CONFIRMED TWICE AND RECORDED AS A RULE: IN THIS CODEBASE A COMMENT ASSERTING AN ARCHITECTURAL FACT IS THE HIGHEST-RISK CONSTRUCT, BECAUSE IT SUPPRESSES THE CHECK THAT WOULD CATCH IT. Both known-wrong comments are PRESENT VERBATIM IN THE SHARED TREE RIGHT NOW. FIRST, include/cygwin/config.h lines 42-49, in the __aarch64__ branch of __getreent: "On Windows ARM64 the TEB pointer is held in tpidr_el0 (and mirrored in the reserved platform register x18). NT_TIB.StackBase lives at offset 8 on every 64-bit Windows target, so this is the exact analogue of the %gs:8 access used above.", followed by the code __asm __volatile__ ("mrs %0, tpidr_el0" : "=r" (__teb)); then ret = *(char **) (__teb + 8);. THE COMMENT IS BACKWARDS — I measured tpidr_el0 as ZERO and x18 as the actual TEB on this host — and the code it justifies dereferences address 0x8, which is precisely the captured access-violation target. NOTE THE SECONDARY CLAIM IS TRUE AND MADE THE WHOLE THING MORE PLAUSIBLE: StackBase really does live at offset 8, which I confirmed by matching [x18+8] against GetCurrentThreadStackLimits exactly. A comment that is half right is more dangerous than one that is wrong throughout. SECOND, local_includes/exception.h lines 14-18: "Note the struct is plain _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT on every architecture -- there is no _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 -- hence the mangled handler name below uses P19_DISPATCHER_CONTEXT, identical to x86_64." That universal is FALSE, as I established earlier by measuring four separate header sets: CLANGARM64 and mingw-w64 master both DEFINE _DISPATCHER_CONTEXT_ARM64 and therefore mangle to P25. THIRD, NEWLY FOUND AND FLAGGED AS UNVERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED WRONG: include/cygwin/exit_process.h line 199 states "However, x86_64 on ARM64 claims not to be WOW64, so we have to ...". This is an architectural assertion about Windows ARM64 process identity of exactly the risky class. It MAY well be accurate for the LEGACY IsWow64Process API, which reports only x86-on-x64 and would indeed answer false for an x64 process on ARM64, while being misleading with respect to IsWow64Process2, which I used earlier and which reports ProcessMachine 0x8664 for exactly that case. I HAVE NOT TESTED IT and am not claiming it is wrong; per the sweep instruction it is flagged as UNVERIFIED UNTIL MEASURED. The remaining hits in the sweep were false positives on the literal 0x18 in unrelated character handling and on an x18 field name in a signal-context struct.

title: TECHNIQUE (reusable): verify a patch applies by PRE-IMAGE BLOB COMPARISON rather than by trial application
description: REUSABLE TECHNIQUE recorded 2026-09-03 at the coordinator request, generalised beyond the case that produced it. TO PROVE A PATCH APPLIES TO A GIVEN COMMIT WITHOUT MUTATING ANYTHING: parse each "index <pre>..<post>" header from the diff, take the file path from the adjacent "+++ b/<path>" line, and compare <pre> against the output of git rev-parse <commit>:<path>, which is the blob the commit actually holds at that path. Abbreviated pre-image hashes compare correctly against the leading characters of the full blob OID. An all-zero pre-image denotes a new file and has no counterpart to check. WHY IT IS BETTER THAN git apply --check: it answers the same question but requires NO CHECKOUT, NO WORKTREE, NO INDEX and NO APPLY, so it CANNOT leave residue, cannot disturb a session in progress, and is safe to run against a repository someone else is using. It is also immune to the line-ending normalisation that makes trial application unreliable on Windows, because blob OIDs are computed over the stored content rather than the worktree bytes. CAVEAT WORTH STATING: this proves the PRE-IMAGES MATCH, which is what determines applicability; it does not prove the post-image content is what anyone intended, so it complements rather than replaces a content review.

title: VERIFIED: the import-library alignment fix is exactly as claimed; .idata$4 risk confirmed real
description: VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-03 for session dfef7f1e (ARM64 import library alignment). ALL CLAIMS HOLD EXACTLY. Comparing the original /root/xc/implibs/lib/libkernel32.a against the patched /root/xc/w-implib/lib/libkernel32.a: both are 1,385,232 bytes, i.e. SIZE IS UNCHANGED, and cmp -l reports EXACTLY 1,642 DIFFERING BYTES, precisely the claimed figure. Every single one of the 1,642 transitions is octal 60 to octal 100, that is 0x30 to 0x40, with NO other transition of any kind — so the patch is exactly as described and touches nothing else. Section-header inspection confirms the intended effect and its limit: in the ORIGINAL, .idata$4 and .idata$5 are BOTH at 2**2 across 1,642 members; in the PATCHED library, .idata$5 is at 2**3 while .idata$4 REMAINS AT 2**2. THE SESSION OWN FLAGGED UNKNOWN IS THEREFORE CONFIRMED AS A REAL, STILL-OPEN ITEM rather than a hypothetical: 1,642 .idata$4 sections are still 4-byte aligned. ASSESSMENT, DERIVED NOT MEASURED: .idata$5 holds the Import Address Table, which generated code loads with LDR Xn, and the IMAGE_REL_ARM64_PAGEOFFSET_12L relocation is a scaled 12-bit offset that requires an 8-byte-aligned target for a 64-bit load — which is exactly why raising .idata$5 to 2**3 eliminated all 10 relocation truncation errors. .idata$4 holds the Import Lookup Table, whose entries are also 8 bytes on PE32+, but it is normally read by the Windows loader rather than addressed by generated code, which plausibly explains why it produced no link error. That makes the residual risk a RUNTIME and IMAGE-LAYOUT question rather than a link-time one, and it remains genuinely unresolved. RECOMMENDATION, NOT ACTIONED AND NOT AUTHORISED: apply the same alignment bump to .idata$4 for consistency, since the cost is identical to the change already made and it removes a class of doubt rather than leaving a silent misalignment in the import tables. NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the before and after relocation-truncation counts of 10 and 0, and the residual 12 sibling-scope errors, all of which come from that session own link run.

The per-symbol check is what established the truth. THE HONEST RISK THEY DISCLOSED IS REAL AND SHOULD BE CARRIED: FPCR trap-enable bits are RAZ/WI on many ARM64 implementations including Windows on Arm, so feenableexcept may not actually enable hardware traps; they note this matches FreeBSD aarch64 behaviour, and disclosing it rather than claiming working traps is the correct call. HAZARD FOUND, NOT PREVIOUSLY REPORTED: /root/xc/w-orphans/gendef2 at 23,862 bytes IS BROKEN — perl fails to compile it with a syntax error at line 47 near "if !", so it aborts and produces nothing. It sits unmarked alongside the working gendef and its higher-numbered name suggests a successor, so anyone selecting it would get a script that does not run. This is the misleading-name discoverability hazard class again. Recommend deleting or clearly marking it.

title: Attempting to verify the ARM64 hardware watchpoint claim - VOID
description: VOID, REPORTED AS VOID RATHER THAN AS A RESULT. c63ab774 claims hardware data watchpoints fail on this platform - missed writes a code breakpoint caught - despite readback confirming Wcr[0]=0x1FF5 and Wvr[0]=0x800000008. That is a platform-capability claim determining instrumentation strategy, so I tried to test it. FOUR ITERATIONS, INSTRUMENT BROKEN A DIFFERENT WAY EACH TIME: (1) armed on the RUNNING CURRENT thread, readback Wcr[0]=0x0, never armed - you cannot set debug registers on a running current thread; (2) re-armed on a properly SUSPENDED thread, readback Wcr[0]=0x0 again; (3) validated CONTEXT offsets and found ContextFlags reading back 0x00000000 AFTER A SUCCESSFUL GetThreadContext, with Sp=0x27f, Pc=0x0, X18=0x0, all nonsense. (3) EXPLAINS (1) AND (2): THE CONTEXT BUFFER WAS NEVER POPULATED because ARM64 CONTEXT REQUIRES 16-BYTE ALIGNMENT and Marshal.AllocHGlobal does not guarantee it. ALL RUNS VOID. I HAVE NO VERDICT on whether ARM64 hardware watchpoints work - cannot confirm, cannot refute. Their readback showed the registers actually set; mine never did, so their arming was real and mine was not. OFFERED INSTEAD, LABELLED AS ARCHITECTURAL REASONING NOT MEASUREMENT: hardware watchpoints on Windows are PER-THREAD since debug registers live in the thread CONTEXT, so a watchpoint armed on thread A cannot observe a store executed by thread B, whereas a code breakpoint patched into the shared instruction stream is process-wide. THAT ASYMMETRY EXACTLY MATCHES THE OBSERVATION. Suggested checking whether the watchpoint was armed on EVERY existing thread and on each new thread at CREATE_THREAD_DEBUG_EVENT before concluding a platform limitation. NOTABLE: MY HARNESS CAUGHT ITS OWN FAILURE THREE TIMES - the readback, the ARMED:False guard, and the ContextFlags check - each of which would otherwise have shipped as a confident wrong platform verdict. The self-check discipline worked; it just kept reporting the instrument was broken, which is why I have nothing to give.
